steps.title: Confirm gate scope on the Jira 'Design Gate' issue
steps.sop: In the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), the Solutions Architect confirms the 'Design Gate' issue for the named release version has the ADR(s) and design package attached and that the scope covers all pull requests targeting the release branch for that release. Done when the issue lists the release version, ADR links, and design package.
steps.verify: Open the Jira 'Design Gate' issue in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if it names the release version and has both the ADR link(s) and the design package attached.

steps.title: Populate the mandatory gate-record fields
steps.sop: In the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), the Software Engineer populates the gate record with all five mandatory fields: ADR link, design-vs-implementation conformance note, CI status (green), SAST/SCA status (0 critical/high findings), and named approver. Done when every field is non-empty and the Jira gate transition is no longer blocked.
steps.verify: Open the gate record on the 'Design Gate' issue; pass if all five fields (ADR link, conformance note, CI status green, SAST/SCA 0 critical/high, named approver) are populated and the workflow permits the gate transition.

steps.title: Reconcile merged PR count against the design package scope table
steps.sop: The Software Engineer counts the pull requests merged to the release branch and compares that count to the number listed on the design package's scope table, recording the reconciliation result on the 'Design Gate' issue in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the counts match exactly; any unlisted PR blocks approval until reconciled.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation note on the 'Design Gate' issue; pass if the merged-PR count equals the scope-table count with zero unexplained deltas, or every delta has a documented resolution.

steps.title: Log each conditional-approval condition as a linked Jira sub-task
steps.sop: If the decision will be Conditional, the Enterprise Architect creates one linked Jira sub-task per condition in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), each with an owner and a due date. Done when every condition has its own sub-task; unresolved conditions at deploy time block promotion via the pipeline gate.
steps.verify: Open the 'Design Gate' issue's linked sub-tasks; pass if every condition named in the decision has a corresponding sub-task with a named owner and due date.

steps.title: Record the signed gate decision on the Design Gate issue
steps.sop: The Enterprise Architect records the gate decision as a comment on the Jira 'Design Gate' issue in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), stating the approver's name, the decision (Approve/Reject/Conditional), any conditions, and an ISO-8601 timestamp, and noting that approval expires if the release is not deployed within 30 calendar days. Done when the comment is posted; it is retained 3 years.
steps.verify: Open the comment thread on the 'Design Gate' issue; pass if a decision comment exists containing approver name, decision value, conditions (if any), an ISO-8601 timestamp, and the 30-calendar-day expiry note.

steps.title: Memorialize the gate decision in Confluence
steps.sop: The Solutions Architect copies the gate decision, the reconciliation result, and links to the ADR(s) and design package onto the release's gate page in Confluence. Done when the Confluence page shows the decision and links back to the Jira 'Design Gate' issue.
steps.verify: Open the release gate page in Confluence; pass if it records the decision, links to the Jira 'Design Gate' issue, and references the ADR(s) and design package.

steps.title: Capture Tech Lead countersign on the gate record
steps.sop: The Enterprise Architect requests the Tech Lead's sign-off on the gate record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the Tech Lead's approval is recorded on the 'Design Gate' issue.
steps.verify: Open the 'Design Gate' issue's approval history; pass if a sign-off entry attributed to the Tech Lead exists with a timestamp after the decision comment.

tasks.taskName: Hand elaborated requirements package to engineering team

steps.title: Assemble the requirements package on the epic
steps.sop: In the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), the Business Analyst gathers the epic's user stories, acceptance criteria, NFRs, and traceability matrix into the handover package, built to the current approved elaboration template / Definition of Ready version. Done when the epic links all four artifact types and names the template version.
steps.verify: Open the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if it links stories, acceptance criteria, NFRs, and a traceability matrix, and references the approved elaboration template version.

steps.title: Validate every story's mandatory fields
steps.sop: The Business Analyst checks each story in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) for a title, description, acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then form, and a priority, with NFRs and dependencies documented. Done when no story in the package is missing acceptance criteria.
steps.verify: Filter the epic's stories in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if 100% of stories have title, description, Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and priority populated.

steps.title: Flag oversized stories for splitting
steps.sop: The Business Analyst flags every story exceeding the size threshold (> 8 story points) in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) for splitting before it can be accepted into the sprint backlog. Done when each oversized story carries the split flag or has been split.
steps.verify: Run a query for stories > 8 points in the package; pass if every result is either flagged for splitting or already decomposed into compliant stories.

steps.title: Complete the traceability reconciliation
steps.sop: The Business Analyst confirms in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) that the count of elaborated requirements equals the count of stories transferred and that the traceability matrix maps each requirement to at least one backlog item. Done when there are 0 unmapped requirements.
steps.verify: Open the traceability matrix; pass if every requirement row maps to >= 1 backlog item and the requirement count equals the transferred story count.

steps.title: Log open questions as 'needs-clarification' items
steps.sop: The Business Analyst logs every open question or unresolved dependency as a Jira item flagged 'needs-clarification' in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), each with an owner and disposition, before the handover completes. Done when no undocumented open question remains.
steps.verify: Query items flagged 'needs-clarification' linked to the epic; pass if each has an owner and disposition, and no open question is mentioned in the package without a matching item.

steps.title: Publish the versioned handover package
steps.sop: The Business Analyst publishes the package to Microsoft 365 / SharePoint; Confluence on the epic's page, recording the package version and transfer timestamp in UTC. Done when the page shows the versioned package and timestamp.
steps.verify: Open the epic's page in Microsoft 365 / SharePoint; Confluence; pass if the handover package is attached with a version identifier and a UTC transfer timestamp.

steps.title: Obtain written engineering acceptance of the handover
steps.sop: The Software Engineer, on behalf of the receiving engineering team, confirms acceptance of the package in writing on the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Stories failing Definition of Ready are returned to the Business Analyst with blocking comments; unresolved gaps become an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Product Owner with a 10-business-day SLA. Done when the acceptance comment is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the epic's comments; pass if a written acceptance from the Software Engineer exists, and any DoR failures are either resolved or tracked in an open 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Product Owner.

steps.title: Capture Tech Lead sign-off on the handover
steps.sop: The Business Analyst requests Tech Lead sign-off on the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); requirements affecting regulated processes or customer PII additionally require joint Product Owner and Tech Lead sign-off. Done when the required sign-off(s) are recorded on the epic.
steps.verify: Open the epic's approval record; pass if Tech Lead sign-off is present, and for regulated/PII-affecting requirements a Product Owner sign-off is also present.

steps.title: Define the applicability assessment scope in the GRC platform
steps.sop: In the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC), the Business Analyst records the assessment scope — the systems, data domains, and jurisdictions named in the intake request — covering data privacy (GDPR/CCPA), cybersecurity (NYDFS 500), and insurance-specific rules, following the enterprise GRC obligations-mapping procedure at its current version. Done when the scope record names all in-scope systems, data domains, and jurisdictions and cites the methodology version.
steps.verify: Open the assessment record in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC); pass if scope lists systems, data domains, and jurisdictions matching the intake request and the register header cites the obligations-mapping procedure version.

steps.title: Catalogue each applicable obligation with full attribution
steps.sop: The Compliance Analyst records each applicable obligation in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC) with: exact rule citation (e.g. 'GDPR Art. 30 RoPA', 'NYDFS 500.16 IR plan', 'CCPA 1798.100 notice at collection'), source regime, jurisdiction, triggering data category or process, control owner, mapped system(s), the internal policy section, and a NIST CSF/ISO 27001 control mapping. Done when no obligation lacks a named owner and control mapping.
steps.verify: Sample 10 catalogued obligations in the GRC platform; pass if each traces to primary regulatory text and every entry has citation, regime, jurisdiction, trigger, control owner, mapped systems, internal policy section, and NIST CSF/ISO 27001 mapping.

steps.title: Reconcile the catalogue against the GRC obligations library
steps.sop: The Compliance Analyst cross-checks the catalogue count against the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC) obligations library for the same scope. Done when the reconciliation shows 0 unaccounted-for in-scope obligations.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation result in the GRC platform; pass if catalogue count matches the obligations-library count for the scope with 0 unexplained differences.

steps.title: Escalate sensitive-data capabilities to a DPIA
steps.sop: The Compliance Analyst flags in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC) any capability touching special-category or otherwise sensitive personal data, triggering a mandatory DPIA before build. Done when each sensitive-data capability has a DPIA record opened.
steps.verify: Query the GRC platform for in-scope capabilities flagged sensitive; pass if every one links to an open or completed DPIA record.

steps.title: Log unmeetable obligations as SDLC-Exception items
steps.sop: In the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), the Business Analyst logs each obligation that cannot be met in-scope as an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket in the regulatory filing/issue tracker with a risk rating and remediation plan, owner = Compliance Lead, tracked to closure with a 10-business-day SLA before baseline sign-off. Done when every gap has a ticket.
steps.verify: Query 'SDLC-Exception' tickets linked to the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if every catalogued cannot-meet obligation has a ticket with risk rating, remediation plan, and Compliance Lead as owner.

steps.title: Record statutory filing deadlines with owners
steps.sop: The Compliance Analyst records every obligation with a statutory filing deadline (e.g. NYDFS annual certification by April 15) in the regulatory filing/issue tracker in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), each with its due date and a named owner. Done when all deadline-bearing obligations are tracked.
steps.verify: Open the regulatory filing tracker; pass if each deadline-bearing obligation from the catalogue appears with due date and owner, including the NYDFS April 15 certification where applicable.

steps.title: Version the register and link it to the Jira epic
steps.sop: The Business Analyst exports the compliance requirements register from the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC), versioned and timestamped, and links it to the Jira epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); evidence is retained per regime (GDPR/CCPA privacy records for the disclosed retention period; NYDFS cybersecurity records minimum 3 years). Done when the epic links the versioned register and the catalogue is complete before the solution architecture document is baselined.
steps.verify: Open the Jira epic; pass if it links a versioned, timestamped register export, and the register's retention labels match the applicable regimes.

steps.title: Obtain Legal Counsel sign-off on the register
steps.sop: The Business Analyst routes the register to Legal Counsel for review and sign-off in the GRC platform (Archer/ServiceNow GRC); obligations rated High (financial penalty or breach-notification exposure) additionally require CISO sign-off before the requirements baseline. Done when the sign-off(s) are recorded and every High-rated obligation has an accepted control approach.
steps.verify: Open the register's approval record; pass if Legal Counsel sign-off is recorded, every High-rated obligation shows an accepted control approach, and CISO sign-off is present for High-rated items.

steps.title: Pull the candidate story population from the backlog
steps.sop: In the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), the Software Engineer pulls the full list of backlog items proposed for the upcoming sprint/PI from the 'DEMAND'/team backlog. Done when 100% of commitment candidates are listed for dependency review; the review is re-run at PI planning and again at sprint planning.
steps.verify: Compare the dependency-review list to the sprint/PI candidate list in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the counts match exactly (100% of candidates included).

steps.title: Evaluate blocks/is-blocked-by links on each candidate story
steps.sop: The Software Engineer, with the Backend Developer and UI Developer, reviews each candidate story's 'blocks'/'is-blocked-by' Jira links in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), covering technical, data, team, and external-vendor dependencies. Done when every candidate story has its links evaluated and findings noted.
steps.verify: Open a sample of candidate stories; pass if each shows evidence of dependency evaluation (reviewed links or an explicit 'no dependencies' note) covering technical, data, team, and vendor categories.

steps.title: Record each blocker as a 'Depends On' link with owner and date
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records every identified blocker as a Jira 'Depends On' link in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), each carrying the owning team and a target resolution date. Done when no identified blocker lacks an owner or target date.
steps.verify: Query all 'Depends On' links on candidate stories; pass if every link names an owning team and a target date — 0 open undated blockers.

steps.title: Register cross-team dependencies on the PPM dependency board
steps.sop: The Software Engineer registers each cross-team or cross-train dependency on the dependency board in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align) so the count of open blocking links reconciles to the board. Done when the board's count matches the Jira blocking-link count.
steps.verify: Compare the open blocking-link count in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) to the dependency board in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align); pass if the counts reconcile exactly.

steps.title: Confirm hard blockers are dated before sprint start
steps.sop: The Software Engineer confirms every hard blocker on a story proposed for commitment has a target resolution date on or before sprint start. Done when 0 committed stories carry an unresolved hard dependency.
steps.verify: Run the commitment-readiness check in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if every committed story's hard blockers have target dates <= sprint start and none is unmanaged.

steps.title: Pull blocked stories from the commitment
steps.sop: The Product Owner removes stories with unresolved hard blockers from the sprint commitment in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) and labels them 'blocked-external'; each is tracked to resolution or descope with its disposition noted per item. Done when no committed story remains blocked.
steps.verify: Query stories labeled 'blocked-external'; pass if each is outside the sprint commitment and carries a disposition note (resolution plan or descope).

steps.title: Raise an SDLC-Exception for undatable cross-team blockers
steps.sop: For any cross-team blocker that cannot be given a date, the Software Engineer raises a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) addressed to the Release Train Engineer with a 10-business-day SLA. Done when every undatable blocker has an exception ticket.
steps.verify: Query 'SDLC-Exception' tickets for the sprint/PI; pass if each undatable cross-team blocker has one, assigned to the Release Train Engineer with the 10-business-day SLA recorded.

steps.title: Record Scrum Master sign-off on the dependency review
steps.sop: The Software Engineer requests the Scrum Master's sign-off on the completed dependency review in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), confirming all committed stories have identified dependencies with owner and target date. Done when the sign-off is recorded on the sprint planning record.
steps.verify: Open the sprint planning record; pass if Scrum Master sign-off is present and dated at or before sprint start.

steps.title: Enumerate integration points from the epic's context diagram
steps.sop: The Software Engineer lists every integration point from the epic's context diagram — internal systems (Guidewire modules, integration layer, data platform), other delivery teams, and external/vendor services — as the dependency population in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), during elaboration before the epic is committed to a sprint. Done when each context-diagram interface appears as a register entry.
steps.verify: Compare the dependency register to the epic's context diagram; pass if every interface on the diagram has a matching register entry and none is missing.

steps.title: Resolve each dependency to a CMDB CI
steps.sop: The Backend Developer resolves each register entry to a configuration item in the CMDB, recording system/team name, CMDB CI id, interface type (API/event/file), direction, owner/contact, and readiness status. Done when no entry is missing an owner or CI reference.
steps.verify: Open the register and spot-check entries against the CMDB; pass if every entry carries a valid CI id, interface type, direction, owner/contact, and readiness status.

steps.title: Reconcile dependency count to resolved CIs
steps.sop: The Software Engineer reconciles the register in the CMDB: count of dependencies equals count of resolved CIs, and each cross-team dependency has a matching Jira link on both teams' boards. Done when both reconciliations are clean.
steps.verify: Run the reconciliation; pass if dependencies = resolved CIs exactly and every cross-team dependency shows paired links on both boards in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira).

steps.title: Flag critical-path and vendor dependencies
steps.sop: The Solutions Architect marks as critical any dependency that would delay the epic by more than 1 sprint if unmet (reviewed at portfolio level), and requires a documented contingency/fallback plan for any single external/vendor dependency on the critical path before commitment. Done when all critical flags and contingency plans are recorded on the register.
steps.verify: Filter the register for critical entries; pass if each >1-sprint-impact dependency is flagged critical and every critical-path vendor dependency links a contingency/fallback plan.

steps.title: Log unresolved dependencies as Jira 'Dependency' items
steps.sop: The Software Engineer logs each unresolved or blocked dependency as a Jira 'Dependency' item in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with owner and target date; cross-team blockers are escalated at scrum-of-scrums and unowned dependencies are flagged to the Integration Architect. Proceeding at risk on an unresolved critical dependency requires an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager with a documented mitigation and 10-business-day review. Done when every unresolved dependency is tracked.
steps.verify: Query 'Dependency' items for the epic; pass if each unresolved dependency has owner + target date, and any at-risk critical dependency has an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager.

steps.title: Publish the versioned dependency register on the epic
steps.sop: The Software Engineer publishes the dependency register as a versioned table attached to the epic in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), with date and author, noting the mapping methodology (context diagram + CMDB traversal + interface catalog review) and its approved version; the snapshot is retained for the life of the initiative and re-validated at sprint planning. Done when the register is attached and versioned.
steps.verify: Open the epic's register attachment; pass if it is versioned with date/author, cites the approved mapping-methodology version, and shows a re-validation entry at sprint planning.

steps.title: Obtain the Integration Architect's independent check
steps.sop: The Solutions Architect routes the register to the Integration Architect for independent re-performance/reasonableness review of the dependency mapping. Done when the Integration Architect's review is recorded on the register.
steps.verify: Open the register's review history; pass if an Integration Architect review entry exists dated before sign-off.

steps.title: Record Tech Lead sign-off on the dependency register
steps.sop: The Software Engineer requests Tech Lead sign-off in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), confirming the register is complete, owner-attributed, with readiness status and critical-path flags. Done when the sign-off is recorded; post-implementation, any integration built but not in the register is back-filled and reviewed against this baseline.
steps.verify: Open the epic's approval record; pass if Tech Lead sign-off is recorded after the Integration Architect review and the register shows 100% of entries with owner, CI, and readiness status.

steps.title: Compile the quarter's source items in Confluence
steps.sop: The Software Engineer compiles all onboarding-feedback survey responses and post-mortem action items closed in the rolling quarter (typically 20-60 source items) onto the gap-register workspace in Confluence, excluding non-engineering L&D topics. Done when every source item for the quarter is listed with its survey/PIR ID.
steps.verify: Open the Confluence source list; pass if it contains every onboarding response and post-mortem action item for the quarter, each with a survey/PIR reference ID.

steps.title: Triage every source item to gap or no-gap
steps.sop: The Software Engineer, with the Backend Developer and UI Developer, triages each source item in Confluence, mapping it to a knowledge gap or explicitly closing it as no-gap. Done when 100% of source items are triaged at quarter close.
steps.verify: Check the triage column on the Confluence source list; pass if every source item shows either a linked gap or an explicit no-gap closure — 0 untriaged items.

steps.title: Record each gap in the Confluence gap register
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records each identified gap in the Confluence gap register with: source (onboarding vs post-mortem), affected topic/system, severity, recurrence count, and proposed remediation (doc, training, or tooling). Done when no gap is logged without a source reference; the register keeps version history, author, and last-updated UTC timestamp.
steps.verify: Open the gap register in Confluence; pass if every entry has source type, topic/system, severity, recurrence count, proposed remediation, and a source reference, with version history visible.

steps.title: Reconcile gaps to source items
steps.sop: The Software Engineer reconciles the register in Confluence: every gap links to >= 1 onboarding survey response or post-mortem action, and the sum of source-tagged gaps equals the register total. Done when the reconciliation balances.
steps.verify: Run the reconciliation on the register; pass if each gap has >= 1 source link and the source-tagged count equals the register total exactly.

steps.title: Raise Jira 'KM-GAP' items for unowned or remediation-driving gaps
steps.sop: The Software Engineer logs gaps without a clear owner or remediation path as Jira 'KM-GAP' items in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with disposition (assigned vs deferred-with-rationale), reviewed next quarter; where a gap drives a doc/tooling change it is also linked to the implementing change ticket. Untriaged sources carry a 10-business-day triage SLA. Done when every such gap has a ticket.
steps.verify: Query 'KM-GAP' items in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if each unowned/deferred gap has one with a disposition, and remediation gaps link their implementing change tickets.

steps.title: Run the pre/post quarter register comparison
steps.sop: The Software Engineer compares the gap register before and after the quarter in Confluence: closed remediations are removed from the open list and any gap that reappears across two quarters is flagged recurring. Done when the comparison is documented on the register.
steps.verify: Open the register's quarter-comparison section; pass if closed items are removed from the open list and two-quarter repeats carry a 'recurring' flag.

steps.title: Distribute the gap summary to engineering leads
steps.sop: The Software Engineer distributes the prioritized gap summary to engineering leads and the enablement team, logging the recipients in the quarterly KM sync notes in Confluence. Done when the recipient list is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the quarterly KM sync notes in Confluence; pass if the gap summary is attached and the recipient list (engineering leads + enablement team) is logged.

steps.title: Record Tech Lead approval of the remediation plan
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains Tech Lead approval (backup approver: Platform Engineering Lead, per the delegation matrix on the ENG Confluence page) of the prioritized gap list and remediation plan, recorded with owner assignments in the KM sync notes in Confluence. Done when the decision and owners are documented.
steps.verify: Open the KM sync notes; pass if the approval is attributed to the Tech Lead (or the documented backup), and every prioritized gap shows a named remediation owner.

steps.title: Create the dead-letter topics for the target consumers
steps.sop: The Data Engineer creates the dead-letter topic(s) for the target consumer group's topics (e.g. the policy-events consumer group) in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent). Done when each in-scope source topic has a paired DLQ topic.
steps.verify: List topics in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent); pass if every in-scope source topic has a corresponding dead-letter topic.

steps.title: Implement the DLQ handler with full failure metadata
steps.sop: The Software Engineer implements the handler in the source code/CI-CD repository so every DLQ record carries: original topic, partition, offset, failure reason, retry count, and first-seen timestamp, with max-retry defaulting to 3 before routing to the DLQ. Done when the handler code is committed on the feature branch.
steps.verify: Open the handler code and a sample DLQ record from a test run; pass if all six metadata fields are populated and the retry ceiling is 3.

steps.title: Add the metadata-defect self-alert to the handler
steps.sop: The Backend Developer adds logic in the source code/CI-CD repository so DLQ records missing failure reason or offset are themselves alerted as a defect in the handler. Done when the self-check is covered by a unit test.
steps.verify: Run the handler's unit suite; pass if a test feeds a metadata-incomplete record and asserts that a defect alert is raised.

steps.title: Run the 10,000-message synthetic poison batch in CI
steps.sop: The Software Engineer runs the CI integration stage in the source code/CI-CD repository against a synthetic set of 10,000 messages including >= 500 crafted poison messages (malformed schema, null keys, oversized payloads) plus valid controls. Done when 100% of poison messages route to the DLQ with correct metadata, 0 valid messages are dropped, 0 consumer crashes occur, and (messages consumed) = (successfully processed) + (routed to DLQ) with delta = 0.
steps.verify: Open the CI integration-test report; pass if poison routing is 100%, valid-message loss is 0, crashes are 0, and the 10,000-message reconciliation balances exactly.

steps.title: Attach the pre/post replay comparison to the PR
steps.sop: The Data Engineer replays the synthetic poison batch before and after the change and attaches the comparison report to the pull request in the source code/CI-CD repository: before = poison messages block/crash the consumer; after = bad messages land in the DLQ while good messages continue. Done when the report is attached to the PR.
steps.verify: Open the PR in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if the pre/post comparison report is attached and shows the after-state routing poison to the DLQ with processing continuing.

steps.title: Configure the quarantine topic and DLQ backlog alert
steps.sop: The Backend Developer configures a secondary quarantine topic in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) for messages that cannot be classified, wires the DLQ depth metric and backlog-threshold alert to the service dashboard with on-call paging, and ensures recurring poison patterns raise an 'SDLC-Exception' item (owner = Engineering Manager) for handler fix within 10 business days. Done when the quarantine topic exists and the alert fires in test.
steps.verify: Inspect the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) config and dashboard; pass if the quarantine topic exists, the DLQ depth alert is bound, and a test breach pages on-call.

steps.title: Archive test evidence to the repository release folder
steps.sop: The Software Engineer stores the poison-message routing report and offset reconciliation as CI artifacts and archives them to the release folder of the source code/CI-CD repository with the commit SHA and timestamp; results are valid only for the RC built from that commit. Done when the artifacts are in the release folder.
steps.verify: Open the release folder in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if the routing report and reconciliation are present, tagged with commit SHA and timestamp.

steps.title: Record Tech Lead sign-off on the merged PR
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains Tech Lead approval on the pull request in the source code/CI-CD repository confirming all acceptance criteria: poison routing with metadata, at-least-once delivery preserved, and the DLQ depth alert wired. Done when the PR shows the approval and is merged.
steps.verify: Open the merged PR; pass if a Tech Lead approving review is present and the merge occurred after the CI evidence steps completed.

tasks.taskName: Implement pipeline retry and failure-recovery handlers

steps.title: Enumerate failure-prone operators across the in-scope DAGs
steps.sop: The Data Engineer lists every task/operator that calls an external system or runs a long-running job across the approx. 40 DAGs feeding Guidewire policy/claims/billing downstream reporting in the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect), excluding sandbox DAGs tagged env=dev, and validates the list against the last 90 days of production run history. Done when the operator inventory is recorded on the design ticket.
steps.verify: Compare the operator inventory to the orchestrator's DAG list; pass if every external-call/long-running operator in the ~40 in-scope DAGs appears and env=dev DAGs are excluded.

steps.title: Configure retry and timeout policy on each operator
steps.sop: The Software Engineer sets, in the DAG definitions in the source code/CI-CD repository, for every failure-prone operator: retries >= 3, retry_delay with exponential backoff (base 60s, max 900s), execution_timeout, and an on_failure_callback wired to the alerting channel; values are checked in and reviewed in the PR. Done when all inventoried operators carry the config.
steps.verify: Open the PR diff in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if every inventoried operator declares retries >= 3, exponential backoff 60s-900s, execution_timeout, and on_failure_callback.

steps.title: Configure the circuit breaker and alert escalation
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer configures the circuit breaker to trip after 5 consecutive failures within a 30-minute window per operator, with alert severity escalating from WARN to CRITICAL when >= 2 business-critical DAGs fail simultaneously; a failure is business-material (page on-call) when it blocks a same-day regulatory or finance feed or delays >= 1000 policy/claims records past the 06:00 SLA. Done when the thresholds are in the checked-in config in the source code/CI-CD repository.
steps.verify: Inspect the checked-in resilience config; pass if the 5-failure/30-minute trip, WARN-to-CRITICAL escalation rule, and materiality paging conditions are all present.

steps.title: Record the Resilience Handler ADR
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records the retry/backoff and circuit-breaker pattern as v2.1 of the platform 'Resilience Handler' standard in an ADR under /docs/adr in the source code/CI-CD repository and references it from each DAG's docstring. Done when the ADR is committed and referenced.
steps.verify: Open /docs/adr in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if the Resilience Handler v2.1 ADR exists and sampled DAG docstrings reference it.

steps.title: Run the staging fault-injection suite
steps.sop: The Data Engineer runs fault injection in staging via the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect) on 10 representative DAGs covering the failure taxonomy (transient network, upstream data-late, downstream timeout, auth expiry, partial-batch failure). Done when 100% of injected transient faults auto-recover within the retry budget, every terminal fault raises exactly one alert plus one incident ticket, and post-retry record counts reconcile with 0 variance for idempotent loads (dedupe key = business natural key, no duplicate rows).
steps.verify: Open the fault-injection test log; pass if 0 unhandled failures, 0 silent failures, 0 duplicate records, and exactly one alert + one incident per terminal fault across the 10 DAGs.

steps.title: Log non-retryable operators as SDLC-Exception items
steps.sop: The Software Engineer logs each operator that cannot support automated retry (non-idempotent external call) as an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket, owner = Engineering Manager, with a linked manual-recovery runbook and a 10-business-day remediation SLA; terminal failures with no runbook get the same treatment. Done when every non-retryable operator is ticketed.
steps.verify: Query 'SDLC-Exception' tickets for the release; pass if every non-idempotent operator from the inventory has one, with runbook link, Engineering Manager owner, and the 10-business-day SLA.

steps.title: Archive delivery evidence with the release tag
steps.sop: The Software Engineer retains the PR merge commit SHA, CI run URL, and fault-injection test log in the source code/CI-CD repository and CI artifact store, tagged with the release version and UTC timestamp, retained 12 months; the Site Reliability Engineer performs the independent reasonableness check on the results. Done when evidence is archived and the SRE check is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the CI artifact store entry for the release tag; pass if commit SHA, CI run URL, and fault-injection log are present with UTC timestamp and the SRE review is noted.

steps.title: Record Tech Lead sign-off with the linked change ticket
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains Tech Lead sign-off on the PR in the source code/CI-CD repository, with the deployment linked to its change ticket (CHG-####) — the change-ticket ID recorded in the CI/CD deploy step and in the DAG version tag. Done when the approval and change-ticket linkage are both recorded.
steps.verify: Open the PR and the deploy step; pass if the Tech Lead approval exists and the CHG-#### ID appears in both the deploy step and the DAG version tag.

steps.title: Register the source-topic schemas in the schema registry
steps.sop: The Data Engineer registers the schema for each in-scope source topic (policy/claims/billing event topics) in the schema registry of the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent). Done when every source topic has a registered schema version.
steps.verify: Query the schema registry in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent); pass if every in-scope source topic resolves to a registered schema with a version number.

steps.title: Author the ingestion job configuration
steps.sop: The Software Engineer commits the job config to the source code/CI-CD repository specifying: source topic/connection, registered schema, checkpoint/offset store, dead-letter topic, and idempotency key; CI validates that all required config keys are present. Done when the config passes CI validation.
steps.verify: Open the CI validation run in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if the config check is green with all five required keys (source, schema, checkpoint store, DLQ topic, idempotency key) present.

steps.title: Implement the Bronze landing logic
steps.sop: The Backend Developer implements the ingestion job in the source code/CI-CD repository so each job reads its named source topic and lands raw records to the Bronze/landing layer of the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse. Done when unit tests for the landing path pass in CI.
steps.verify: Run the CI unit suite; pass if landing-path tests are green and a test-environment run shows records from the source topic arriving in the Bronze/landing layer of the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse.

steps.title: Wire malformed records to the dead-letter topic
steps.sop: The Data Engineer wires the job so malformed or unprocessable records route to the dead-letter topic in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) and are logged. Done when a crafted malformed record lands in the DLQ during test.
steps.verify: Publish a malformed test record; pass if it appears on the dead-letter topic in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) with a log entry, and is absent from Bronze.

steps.title: Run the 24-hour non-prod soak
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer runs the job continuously against the source topics in the non-prod environment for >= 24 hours. Done when the soak completes with no unhandled failures and consumer-lag plus landed-count delta <= 0.1%.
steps.verify: Open the soak-test run logs; pass if the job ran >= 24 hours unbroken, 0 unhandled failures, and the lag/landed-count delta is <= 0.1%.

steps.title: Reconcile consumed vs landed record counts
steps.sop: The Data Engineer reconciles records consumed from each source topic against records landed in Bronze in the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse within the watermark window, and raises a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' (owner = Data Engineer, 5-business-day remediation SLA) for any sustained lag or DLQ growth. Done when the reconciliation is within tolerance and any breach is ticketed.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation query output; pass if consumed = landed within the watermark window at <= 0.1% delta, and any breach shows a linked 'SDLC-Exception' ticket.

steps.title: Commit the job manifest and soak evidence
steps.sop: The Software Engineer commits the job manifest, schema version, and soak-test run logs to the source code/CI-CD repository, retained with the build artifact, with the pipeline run id and timestamp recorded in the CI/CD system. Done when the evidence is attached to the build.
steps.verify: Open the build artifact in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if manifest, schema version, and soak logs are attached with run id and timestamp.

steps.title: Record DevOps Engineer sign-off
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains the DevOps Engineer's sign-off on the ingestion job release in the source code/CI-CD repository, confirming the 24-hour soak and reconciliation evidence. Done when the approval is recorded on the PR/release.
steps.verify: Open the PR/release record; pass if DevOps Engineer approval is present and dated after the soak evidence was attached.

steps.title: Author the transform job configuration
steps.sop: The Software Engineer commits the transform config to the source code/CI-CD repository specifying: input Bronze source, output schema, windowing/watermark strategy, data-quality rules, and error/DLQ handling; CI validates all required transform parameters are present. Done when the config passes CI validation.
steps.verify: Open the CI validation run in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if all five parameter groups (input, output schema, windowing/watermark, DQ rules, DLQ handling) are present and the check is green.

steps.title: Implement the Bronze-to-Silver transform logic
steps.sop: The Backend Developer implements the cleansing, enrichment, and business-rule transforms in the source code/CI-CD repository, reading Bronze/landing records and producing Silver/curated output topics or tables in the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse. Done when the transform code compiles and its unit tests pass.
steps.verify: Run the CI unit suite; pass if transform tests are green and a test run shows Silver output produced in the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse from Bronze input.

steps.title: Route data-quality failures to the quarantine/DLQ table
steps.sop: The Data Engineer wires records failing DQ rules to a quarantine/DLQ table with reason codes, publishing error events via the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) where applicable. Done when a crafted DQ-failing record lands in quarantine with its reason code.
steps.verify: Feed a DQ-failing test record; pass if it appears in the quarantine/DLQ table with a populated reason code and is absent from Silver output.

steps.title: Commit unit and integration test results
steps.sop: The QA Analyst runs and commits the unit/integration test results for the transforms to the source code/CI-CD repository, retained with the artifact. Done when the test report is green and attached to the build.
steps.verify: Open the build in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if the unit/integration test report is attached and all tests pass.

steps.title: Run the 24-hour soak with record-conservation check
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer runs the transform job continuously against ingested streams in non-prod for >= 24 hours. Done when input record count reconciles to output + filtered + DLQ counts (conservation of records) within 0.1% and sampled row-level checksums confirm enrichment accuracy.
steps.verify: Open the soak report; pass if the job ran >= 24 hours producing validated output, the conservation equation balances within 0.1%, and sampled checksums match.

steps.title: Ticket recurring data-quality failures
steps.sop: The Data Engineer raises a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' (owner = Data Engineer, 5-business-day remediation SLA) for any recurring DQ-rule failure pattern observed during the soak. Done when every recurring pattern has a ticket.
steps.verify: Review the quarantine reason-code distribution against open tickets; pass if each recurring failure pattern has a matching 'SDLC-Exception' with the 5-business-day SLA.

steps.title: Commit soak lineage evidence with the artifact
steps.sop: The Software Engineer commits the soak-test lineage and run evidence to the source code/CI-CD repository, with run id and timestamp recorded in the CI/CD system. Done when the lineage evidence is retained with the build artifact.
steps.verify: Open the build artifact; pass if soak lineage, run id, and timestamp are attached.

steps.title: Record QA Analyst sign-off
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains the QA Analyst's sign-off on the transform release in the source code/CI-CD repository, confirming output validity and the conservation reconciliation. Done when the approval is recorded on the PR/release.
steps.verify: Open the PR/release record; pass if QA Analyst approval is present and dated after the soak evidence was committed.

tasks.taskName: Incorporate feedback into platform improvement cycles

steps.title: Consolidate feedback themes for the cycle
steps.sop: The Software Engineer consolidates developer feedback from the DevEx survey, retros, and platform support tickets into themes in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) within 2 weeks of the survey/retro close. Done when every raw feedback item for the cycle is assigned to a theme.
steps.verify: Open the cycle's theme list; pass if every source feedback item maps to a theme and consolidation happened within 2 weeks of close.

steps.title: Score each theme with the approved impact x reach method
steps.sop: The Platform Engineering Lead scores each theme using the impact x reach prioritization method at the version approved in the platform backlog policy, with scoring parameters sourced from that policy (not ad-hoc); scores are recalculated when new feedback volume shifts reach estimates. Done when every theme carries impact, reach, and priority scores.
steps.verify: Open the scored theme list; pass if every theme has impact and reach values, the policy version is referenced, and priorities derive from the documented parameters.

steps.title: Create a tagged Jira item per actioned theme
steps.sop: The Software Engineer creates one Jira item per actioned theme in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with: source reference, problem statement, priority, owner, and target increment, tagged 'devex-feedback' and linked back to the originating survey/retro. Done when every actioned theme has a complete item.
steps.verify: Query items tagged 'devex-feedback' for the cycle; pass if each has source reference, problem statement, priority, owner, and target increment, and links to its originating survey/retro.

steps.title: Document declines with rationale and feedback loop
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records a documented decline rationale in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) for every theme not actioned and communicates it back to developers; disputed declines escalate to the Platform Engineering Lead for review. Done when no theme is silently dropped.
steps.verify: Review non-actioned themes; pass if each carries a written decline rationale and a record of the communication back to developers.

steps.title: Reconcile themes to backlog items and declines
steps.sop: The Platform Engineering Lead reconciles in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira): count of triaged feedback themes = backlog items created + explicit declines, with delta = 0 and no theme untriaged after the cycle; the DevOps / Platform Automation Engineer independently re-performs the check. Done when the reconciliation balances.
steps.verify: Run the reconciliation; pass if themes = items + declines exactly (delta 0), 0 untriaged themes, and the independent re-performance is recorded.

steps.title: Schedule material themes into the increment roadmap
steps.sop: The Platform Engineering Lead schedules qualifying themes into the current increment in the product roadmap/backlog tool; only themes affecting >= 3 squads or a top-3 DevEx pain point qualify for the current increment, with smaller items parked in the backlog with a tag. Done when top themes appear in the increment plan.
steps.verify: Open the increment plan in the product roadmap/backlog tool; pass if every scheduled theme meets the >= 3 squads or top-3 pain-point bar and parked items carry the backlog tag.

steps.title: Record the feedback-to-backlog mapping for the cycle
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records the mapping (theme -> Jira key or decline rationale) in the product roadmap/backlog tool with cycle ID and UTC timestamp, retained 12 months, with each backlog item retaining its source link. Done when the mapping is published.
steps.verify: Open the cycle's mapping record; pass if every theme resolves to a Jira key or decline rationale, stamped with cycle ID and UTC timestamp.

steps.title: Record Platform Engineering Lead sign-off on the cycle
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains the Platform Engineering Lead's sign-off on the completed triage cycle in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the sign-off is recorded against the cycle record.
steps.verify: Open the cycle record; pass if Platform Engineering Lead sign-off is present and dated after the reconciliation balanced.

steps.title: Set the sprint goal and dates on the Jira board
steps.sop: The Scrum Master creates the sprint on the Jira board in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with a named goal and the 2-week start/end dates, scoped to the approved epic(s); sprint start is blocked until the goal field is set and at least 1 committed story exists. Done when the sprint record shows goal and dates.
steps.verify: Open the sprint in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the goal field is populated, start/end dates span 2 weeks, and the sprint is linked to the approved epic(s).

steps.title: Screen candidate stories against Definition of Ready
steps.sop: The Product Owner reviews each of the proposed stories (typically 8-15) in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) against the Definition of Ready; stories not meeting DoR are excluded and returned to the backlog with a 'Not Ready' label and a reason note. Done when every candidate is either DoR-compliant or returned.
steps.verify: Query the sprint's stories and the 'Not Ready' returns; pass if 0 not-ready stories are committed and each returned story carries the label plus a reason note.

steps.title: Commit stories with estimates, owners, and pipeline links
steps.sop: The Software Engineer, with the Backend Developer and UI Developer, ensures each committed story in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) has an estimate, an assigned owner, and a linked repository/CI pipeline. Done when no committed story is missing any of the three.
steps.verify: Inspect each committed story; pass if 100% have estimate, assignee, and repository/CI pipeline link.

steps.title: Reconcile commitment against team velocity
steps.sop: The Scrum Master reconciles capacity vs commitment at planning in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira): the sum of committed story points must be <= the team's rolling 3-sprint average velocity +/- 15%; if capacity < commitment, scope is reduced at planning and unresolved blockers are escalated to the Scrum Master and Product Owner the same day. Done when commitment is within the velocity band.
steps.verify: Compare committed points to the 3-sprint average velocity; pass if the total is within +/- 15% of velocity and any overage shows a documented scope reduction.

steps.title: Record the sprint commitment in the PPM tool
steps.sop: The Scrum Master records the sprint commitment and planning minutes in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align) for portfolio visibility, timestamped at sprint start. Done when the commitment record is saved.
steps.verify: Open the sprint's record in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align); pass if the commitment and planning summary are recorded with a timestamp at or before sprint start.

steps.title: Start the sprint in Jira
steps.sop: The Scrum Master starts the sprint in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when an active sprint exists with a documented goal, committed DoR-compliant stories, and assigned engineers, and the Jira sprint report is generating.
steps.verify: Open the Jira sprint report; pass if the sprint is active, shows the goal, and every committed story meets DoR with an assignee.

steps.title: Record Product Owner sign-off on the sprint commitment
steps.sop: The Scrum Master captures the Product Owner's sign-off on the sprint commitment in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the sign-off is recorded on the sprint record at sprint start.
steps.verify: Open the sprint record's approval trail; pass if Product Owner sign-off is present, timestamped at sprint start.

steps.title: Enumerate integration points from the dependency manifest
steps.sop: The Software Engineer lists all new/changed integration points — REST/gRPC clients, Kafka producer/consumer bindings, and DB connections — declared in the service's dependency manifest (build.gradle/pom.xml/package.json) and its OpenAPI 3.0 spec in the source code/CI-CD repository, excluding third-party SaaS webhooks handled by MuleSoft. Done when the integration inventory is recorded on the story.
steps.verify: Compare the inventory to the manifest and OpenAPI spec in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if every declared client/binding/connection appears and MuleSoft-handled webhooks are excluded.

steps.title: Externalize endpoint configuration with resilience policies
steps.sop: The Backend Developer externalizes, in the source code/CI-CD repository, every downstream endpoint's base URL, timeout, and retry/circuit-breaker policy to config (no hardcoded hosts): retries capped at 3 with exponential backoff, circuit opens at 50% error rate over a 30s window, p95 downstream latency budget 200ms. Done when config review in the PR confirms all endpoints comply.
steps.verify: Open the PR diff; pass if no hardcoded hosts remain and each endpoint declares timeout, retry cap 3 with backoff, and the 50%/30s circuit-breaker threshold.

steps.title: Pin API versions per the deprecation policy
steps.sop: The Software Engineer pins each consumed API version in the source code/CI-CD repository per the twelve-month deprecation policy, records the pins in the service README, and references the approved solution architecture document (SAD) version and ADR from the story. Done when the README lists every pinned version.
steps.verify: Open the service README; pass if every consumed API has a pinned version consistent with the SAD/ADR reference on the story.

steps.title: Wire consumer-driven contract tests to the schema registry
steps.sop: The Backend Developer wires contract tests in the source code/CI-CD repository validating all required request/response fields against the consumer-driven contracts, with schemas pulled from registered, version-pinned schema-registry entries (subject + version recorded in service config). Done when the contract suite runs in CI with 0 unresolved failures.
steps.verify: Open the CI contract-test run; pass if 100% of contract tests are green and the service config records subject + version for each schema.

steps.title: Run the staging integration smoke suite
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer runs the integration smoke in staging via the source code/CI-CD repository pipeline: 20 synthetic transactions covering happy path, downstream timeout, and malformed payload. Done when request count in = response count out across each wired dependency, Kafka consumer offsets reconcile to 0 lag, p95 latency <= 200ms, and 0 unhandled exceptions; integrations handling policy/claims financial transactions additionally show 90% test coverage and a completed load test.
steps.verify: Open the staging smoke-test report attached to the CI build; pass if in/out counts balance per dependency, offset lag is 0, p95 <= 200ms, 0 unhandled exceptions, and critical-path integrations meet the 90% coverage + load-test bar.

steps.title: Trace five sample transactions end-to-end
steps.sop: The Software Engineer traces 5 sample transactions from the calling component through each dependency to the persisted record in the target system, capturing correlation IDs at each hop, and verifies state transitions (pending/committed/failed/compensated) align to the Saga workflow in the SAD with compensating actions firing on downstream failure, and that createdAt/processedAt timestamps are UTC and monotonic with no clock-skew gap exceeding 2s. Done when all 5 traces are documented.
steps.verify: Open the trace evidence; pass if 5 transactions show unbroken correlation IDs across hops, Saga-conformant state transitions with compensation on failure, and UTC-monotonic timestamps within 2s skew.

steps.title: Store CI evidence and route failures to defects
steps.sop: The Software Engineer stores the CI pipeline run URL, commit SHA, and integration-test report (JUnit XML) as build artifacts in the source code/CI-CD repository, retained 12 months and tagged with the Jira story key; failed contract/integration tests are logged as Jira defects linked to the story and gate the merge, with the waiver path being an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager (10-business-day remediation SLA). Done when the artifacts are tagged and any failures ticketed.
steps.verify: Open the build artifacts; pass if run URL, SHA, and JUnit XML are present tagged with the story key, and every test failure has a linked defect or an approved 'SDLC-Exception'.

steps.title: Obtain the Integration Engineer's independent re-performance
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer independently re-performs or reasonableness-checks the integration verification (contract + smoke results) and records the outcome on the story. Done when the independent check is documented.
steps.verify: Open the story's review history; pass if an Integration Engineer re-performance entry exists dated after the smoke run.

steps.title: Record Tech Lead sign-off on the integration
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains Tech Lead sign-off on the integration PR in the source code/CI-CD repository before the PI increment code-freeze date. Done when the approval is recorded and the wiring is merged.
steps.verify: Open the merged PR; pass if Tech Lead approval is present and the merge date precedes the code-freeze date.

tasks.taskName: Investigate and resolve late or failed pipelines

steps.title: Acknowledge the pipeline alert in Grafana
steps.sop: The Software Engineer acknowledges the late/failed-pipeline alert in Grafana (thresholds: warn at 50% of the SLA window elapsed with the job still running, page on-call at 80%; late-data threshold = watermark lag > 30 min for P1, > 2 h for P2). Done when the alert is acknowledged and the affected run identified.
steps.verify: Open the alert history in Grafana; pass if the alert shows an acknowledgement with responder and time within the paging threshold window.

steps.title: Open the incident with SLA tier and lineage scope
steps.sop: The Software Engineer opens (or claims) the incident in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), recording the SLA tier (P1 finance/regulatory, P2 analytics, P3 internal) and scoping it to the failed/late run plus every downstream dependent job in the same lineage. Done when the incident lists the affected run and downstream scope.
steps.verify: Open the incident; pass if it names the failed run, its SLA tier, and the downstream lineage jobs in scope.

steps.title: Execute recovery per the approved runbook revision
steps.sop: The Data Engineer executes the recovery steps matching the latest approved runbook revision, referenced by id in the incident, using scheduler config and connection parameters sourced only from the version-controlled IaC repo and the secrets vault — no manual parameter overrides permitted during recovery. Done when the pipeline is re-run and caught up to the current watermark.
steps.verify: Compare the executed steps in the incident worklog to the referenced runbook revision; pass if steps match the approved revision and no manual parameter overrides appear.

steps.title: Reconcile post-recovery record counts in the lakehouse
steps.sop: The Data Engineer runs the reconciliation in the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse: post-recovery row counts and control totals for the re-run must match the source watermark with 0 variance for financial feeds and <= 0.1% for analytics feeds, attaching the query result to the incident. Done when the reconciliation is clean and attached.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation attachment on the incident; pass if variance is 0 for financial feeds and <= 0.1% for analytics feeds against the source watermark.

steps.title: Complete the mandatory incident fields
steps.sop: The Software Engineer completes the incident record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with: failed job id, run timestamp, error class (data/infra/dependency), SLA tier, root cause, and recovery action — all mandatory fields non-null before the ticket can be resolved, plus attached scheduler run log, error stack trace, and pipeline commit SHA (retained per the 3-year audit retention). Done when the record passes mandatory-field validation.
steps.verify: Open the incident; pass if all six mandatory fields are populated, the scheduler log and stack trace are attached, and the pipeline commit SHA is recorded.

steps.title: Log the SLA-breach disposition and escalations
steps.sop: The Software Engineer logs the breach disposition on the incident (recovered / re-run / data-quarantine / permanent-fail-escalated); if unresolved within the SLA tier the incident escalates to on-call SRE and the data product owner, and on persistent failure the partial output is quarantined, a P1 'SDLC-Exception' is opened (owner = Engineering Manager, 10-business-day RCA SLA), and downstream consumers are notified via the ITSM broadcast. Done when the disposition and any escalations are recorded.
steps.verify: Open the incident; pass if a disposition value is set and, for persistent failures, the quarantine note, P1 'SDLC-Exception', and broadcast notification are all present.

steps.title: Verify recovery met the SLA tier
steps.sop: The Software Engineer verifies against the incident timeline that recovery met its tier (P1 <= 2 h, P2 <= 8 h, P3 next business day) with downstream jobs green; a missed P1 SLA or > 0 reconciliation variance on a material (regulatory/GL) feed requires data product owner sign-off before close. Done when the timing check is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the incident timeline; pass if recovery duration is within the tier window and downstream jobs show green, or the material-feed data product owner sign-off is attached.

steps.title: Record Release / Environment Manager sign-off and close
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains the Release / Environment Manager's independent check and sign-off on the resolved incident in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the sign-off is recorded and the incident is closed.
steps.verify: Open the closed incident; pass if Release / Environment Manager sign-off is recorded with all evidence attached at the incident record URL.

steps.title: Create the demand record via the intake catalog item
steps.sop: The Demand Manager creates the demand record through the ServiceNow Demand catalog item 'IT Demand Intake' in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); standard operational incidents are out of scope. Done when the record exists with an auto-assigned unique DMND number and creation timestamp.
steps.verify: Open the record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if it was created via the 'IT Demand Intake' catalog item and carries a unique DMND number with an auto-timestamp.

steps.title: Populate the mandatory demand fields
steps.sop: The Business Analyst populates the record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with: requester, sponsoring business unit, problem statement, desired outcome, affected application (CMDB CI reference), and priority; ServiceNow mandatory-field validation blocks submission if any are blank. Done when the record submits cleanly.
steps.verify: Open the demand record; pass if all six mandatory fields are populated, including a resolvable CMDB CI reference, and the record shows a successful submission.

steps.title: Capture requester acknowledgement
steps.sop: The Demand Manager sends the intake confirmation to the requester from the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) and captures the acknowledgement on the demand record. Done when the acknowledgement is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the record's activity log; pass if the confirmation notification and the requester's acknowledgement are both present.

steps.title: Run the daily intake-to-record reconciliation
steps.sop: The Business Analyst reconciles daily in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira): the number of intake emails/forms received in the shared queue equals the number of ServiceNow demand records created. Done when there are 0 unlogged requests older than 1 business day.
steps.verify: Compare the shared-queue count to the demand-record count for the day; pass if they match and no unlogged request is older than 1 business day.

steps.title: Return incomplete requests for clarification
steps.sop: The Demand Manager sets incomplete or out-of-scope requests to state 'Clarification Needed' in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with a work note stating the gap, returning them to the requester with a 3-business-day SLA to re-submit; items unresolved beyond 5 business days escalate to the Demand Manager/PMO. Done when every incomplete request carries the state, note, and SLA clock.
steps.verify: Query records in 'Clarification Needed'; pass if each has a gap work note, requester notification, and any item aged > 5 business days shows a PMO escalation.

steps.title: Export the quarterly demand register to the PPM tool
steps.sop: The Demand Manager exports the quarter's demand records from the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) to the demand register in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align); ServiceNow retains the full audit history (created/updated by/on) for 3 years. Done when the quarterly export is loaded.
steps.verify: Open the demand register in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align); pass if the current quarter's records are present and counts match the ServiceNow export.

steps.title: Record Product Owner sign-off on intake completeness
steps.sop: The Demand Manager obtains the Product Owner's sign-off in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) confirming intake completeness for the period — target >= 98% of records complete on first logging with requester, business unit, outcome, CMDB CI, and priority populated. Done when the sign-off is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the period's intake review record; pass if Product Owner sign-off is present and the completeness measure meets the >= 98% first-logging target.

steps.title: Review all active items on the Demand Pipeline board
steps.sop: The Demand Manager reviews every active demand item (statuses New/Triage/Analysis/Blocked) on the saved Jira board 'Demand Pipeline' in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when 100% of open items have been inspected in the weekly pass.
steps.verify: Open the 'Demand Pipeline' board; pass if the review log covers every open item at the weekly reconciliation cut (100% inspection).

steps.title: Update status, priority, and owner on every row
steps.sop: The Business Analyst updates each register row in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) so it has non-null Status, Priority (P1-P4), Assigned Owner, and Last-Updated date, and no item sits in 'Analysis' older than 30 days without a status update; field definitions follow the Jira admin field configuration for project DEMAND. Done when no mandatory field is null.
steps.verify: Run a JQL check on project DEMAND open items; pass if 0 rows have null Status/Priority/Owner/Last-Updated and no 'Analysis' item exceeds 30 days without an update.

steps.title: Flag and disposition stale items
steps.sop: The Demand Manager ensures items untouched for more than 10 business days are auto-flagged 'register-stale' in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); each flagged item's owner must update or re-triage it within 3 business days with the disposition logged in the item comment. Done when every stale flag has a disposition or an active 3-day clock.
steps.verify: Query items flagged 'register-stale'; pass if each shows a disposition comment or is within its 3-business-day window, and stale items are <= 5% of open items.

steps.title: Run the weekly register-to-Jira reconciliation
steps.sop: The Business Analyst runs the weekly reconciliation via saved JQL export in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira): register item count vs the Jira REST count for project=DEMAND AND statusCategory!=Done. Done when the delta is exactly 0.
steps.verify: Compare the register export row count to the Jira REST count endpoint result; pass if the counts match exactly (delta = 0).

steps.title: Export the weekly register snapshot
steps.sop: The Demand Manager exports the weekly register snapshot (CSV + PDF) from the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) to the compliance evidence repository with export timestamp and generating user; prior snapshots are retained 12 months. Done when the snapshot is stored.
steps.verify: Open the compliance evidence repository; pass if this week's CSV + PDF snapshot exists with timestamp and generating user, and the trailing 12 months of snapshots are present.

steps.title: Escalate reconciliation failures via SDLC-Exception
steps.sop: On a failed check (> 5% stale items or any null mandatory field), the Demand Manager generates a gap list in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), assigns each stale/incomplete item to its owner, and escalates items unresolved after 3 business days to the PMO Manager via a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' ticket with a 10-day SLA. Done when every gap is assigned or escalated.
steps.verify: Open the gap list and linked tickets; pass if each gap item has an owner assignment, and any item aged > 3 business days shows an 'SDLC-Exception' to the PMO Manager.

steps.title: Record Product Owner sign-off on register currency
steps.sop: The Demand Manager obtains the Product Owner's sign-off (register owner per the RACI on the 'Demand Governance' page; delegation to the Scrum Master permitted during PO absence and recorded in the delegation log with start/end dates) in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the weekly sign-off is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the weekly review record; pass if sign-off is attributed to the Product Owner or a logged delegate with valid delegation dates.

steps.title: Draft the quarterly workstation standard update in Confluence
steps.sop: The Software Engineer drafts the quarterly update of the workstation standard in Confluence, specifying OS version, required security agents (EDR, disk encryption), the approved IDE/tool list with versions, and configuration baselines. Done when the draft covers all four specification areas.
steps.verify: Open the draft standard in Confluence; pass if OS version, EDR + disk-encryption agents, versioned IDE/tool list, and configuration baselines are all specified.

steps.title: Attribute every tooling catalogue entry
steps.sop: The Backend Developer assigns an owner and approval status to every entry in the approved tooling catalogue in Confluence. Done when no catalogue entry lacks either field.
steps.verify: Scan the tooling catalogue; pass if 100% of entries carry an owner and an approval status.

steps.title: Reconcile the catalogue against deployed-software inventory
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer reconciles the count of approved tools in the catalogue with the software-inventory/CMDB deployment counts via the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), flagging unmanaged or out-of-catalogue installs for remediation; the deployed fleet must match the standard within 5% drift. Done when the reconciliation report is produced and remediation tickets opened for non-compliant workstations.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation report; pass if catalogue vs deployment counts are reconciled, drift is <= 5%, and every out-of-catalogue install has a remediation ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira).

steps.title: Log tooling exceptions with justification and expiry
steps.sop: The Software Engineer logs each approved exception (non-standard tools, elevated privileges) in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with owner, justification, and expiry date. Done when every deviation from the standard has an exception record.
steps.verify: Query workstation exceptions in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if each has owner, justification, and a future or tracked expiry date.

steps.title: Record the standard-change decision in the CAB change record
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records the standard-change decision in the CAB/ITSM change record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with rationale and approver, referencing the security review outcome; the authorized approver for standard changes is the Platform Engineering Lead per the ITSM change policy's delegation matrix. Done when the change record is complete.
steps.verify: Open the CAB change record; pass if it contains decision, rationale, security-review reference, and the Platform Engineering Lead (or delegated backup) as approver.

steps.title: Publish the versioned standard in Confluence
steps.sop: The Software Engineer publishes the updated standard and tooling catalogue in Confluence with UTC timestamp and change author, archiving the prior version. Done when the new version is live and the old one archived.
steps.verify: Open the standard page in Confluence; pass if the current version shows UTC timestamp and author, is dated within the last quarter, and the prior version is in the archive.

steps.title: Broadcast the updated standard to engineering staff
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer communicates the updated standard to all engineering staff via the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) broadcast and the Confluence notification, with the recipient list being all Software/Backend/UI engineers. Done when the broadcast is sent and recipients documented.
steps.verify: Open the broadcast record; pass if it was sent to the full engineering recipient list and the Confluence notification is logged.

steps.title: Record Platform Engineering Lead sign-off on the standard
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains the Platform Engineering Lead's sign-off on the published standard in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); unresolved compliance exceptions escalate to the Platform Engineering Lead with a 10-business-day SLA. Done when the sign-off is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the standard's approval record; pass if Platform Engineering Lead sign-off is present and dated after publication.

steps.title: Validate catalog-info.yaml files in CI
steps.sop: The Backend Developer ensures every service's catalog-info.yaml validates against the portal catalog schema in the CI stage of the source code/CI-CD repository. Done when the validation job is green for all onboarded services.
steps.verify: Open the CI validation run in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if 0 catalog-info.yaml files fail schema validation.

steps.title: Complete required metadata on every catalog entry
steps.sop: The Software Engineer ensures each catalog entry in Backstage has an owning team, lifecycle state, on-call/runbook link, repo link, and tier, per the catalog-info.yaml specification referenced in the contributor guide. Done when 0 services lack an owner.
steps.verify: Audit the Backstage catalog; pass if every entry shows owner, lifecycle, on-call/runbook link, repo link, and tier — 0 ownerless services.

steps.title: Onboard newly deployed services within one sprint
steps.sop: The UI Developer adds every newly deployed production service to the Backstage catalog within one sprint of its first deploy. Done when no production service deployed more than one sprint ago is missing from the catalog.
steps.verify: Compare recent first-deploy dates to catalog registration dates in Backstage; pass if every new service was catalogued within one sprint of first deploy.

steps.title: Run the monthly CMDB reconciliation
steps.sop: The Platform Engineering Lead runs the monthly reconciliation of the Backstage service count against the CMDB production-service inventory, requiring a variance of +/- 0; discrepancies (in CMDB but not the portal, or vice versa) are raised as ServiceNow tickets to the owning team, with the escalation path an 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Platform Engineering Lead on a 10-business-day SLA. Done when the reconciliation report is published to the platform dashboard.
steps.verify: Open the monthly reconciliation report on the platform dashboard; pass if portal count = CMDB production count, or every delta has an open ticket/exception.

steps.title: Smoke-test one scaffolder per template family
steps.sop: The Backend Developer executes one self-service scaffolder run end-to-end per template family in Backstage. Done when every template family has a passing smoke run this cycle.
steps.verify: Open the scaffolder run history in Backstage; pass if each template family shows a successful end-to-end run within the current cycle — 0 broken scaffolders.

steps.title: Apply all portal changes via reviewed GitOps PRs
steps.sop: The Software Engineer makes every portal configuration change through a reviewed pull request in the source code/CI-CD repository (GitOps), each with commit SHA and author, with deployment records retained 12 months in the CI/CD system; bad portal changes are rolled back via GitOps. Done when no portal config change exists outside a reviewed PR.
steps.verify: Audit the GitOps repo history against portal config state; pass if every change traces to a reviewed PR and rollbacks (if any) are themselves PRs.

steps.title: Record Platform Engineering Lead sign-off on portal currency
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains the Platform Engineering Lead's sign-off confirming every production service is resolvable in Backstage with owner and runbook and that self-service templates execute successfully. Done when the sign-off is recorded with the monthly reconciliation evidence.
steps.verify: Open the monthly sign-off record; pass if Platform Engineering Lead approval is present, referencing the GitOps history and the CMDB reconciliation report.

steps.title: Reconcile the DAG inventory against published runbooks
steps.sop: The Software Engineer reconciles the count of active production DAGs/jobs (Airflow/Control-M/ADF, excluding decommissioned pipelines) against published runbooks in Confluence monthly using the orchestration inventory export. Done when there are 0 orphan pipelines and 0 orphan runbooks.
steps.verify: Open the monthly reconciliation; pass if production DAG count equals published runbook count with every pipeline mapping to exactly one current runbook.

steps.title: Author each runbook to the RB-2.1 template
steps.sop: The Data Engineer authors or updates each runbook in Confluence to template version 'RB-2.1' with: pipeline name, schedule, upstream/downstream dependencies, owner, alert-to-runbook link, and step-by-step recovery for timeout/retry/data-late failures. Done when every runbook conforms to the template structure.
steps.verify: Sample runbooks in Confluence; pass if each follows RB-2.1 and contains all six required sections including the three failure-scenario recovery procedures.

steps.title: Update runbooks within 5 days of any orchestration change
