steps.sop: The Backend Developer updates the affected runbook in Confluence within 5 business days of any orchestration change or post-incident action item, diffing the runbook pre/post so a reviewer confirms recovery steps still match the new DAG topology. Done when the diff and reviewer confirmation are recorded.
steps.verify: Pick recent orchestration changes; pass if each affected runbook was updated within 5 business days and shows a reviewed pre/post diff.

steps.title: Link each runbook update to its triggering ticket
steps.sop: The Software Engineer links each runbook update to the triggering change/incident ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), recorded in the runbook's change-history header. Done when every update row cites a ticket.
steps.verify: Open runbook change-history headers; pass if every update lists the triggering change/incident ticket reference.

steps.title: Log stale or missing runbooks as RUNBOOK-GAP items
steps.sop: The Software Engineer logs stale or missing runbooks as Jira 'RUNBOOK-GAP' items in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with disposition (authored/updated vs decommission-confirmed) and a 5-business-day remediation SLA. Done when every gap from the reconciliation has a ticket.
steps.verify: Query 'RUNBOOK-GAP' items; pass if each reconciliation gap has one with disposition and SLA, and none is older than 5 business days without action.

steps.title: Run the quarterly game-day validation for tier-1 runbooks
steps.sop: The Data Engineer runs a game-day dry-run in staging for each tier-1 critical pipeline runbook (typically 15-40 per quarter, pipelines feeding regulatory/financial reporting), following the runbook verbatim without the author present; recovery must complete within the documented RTO; tier-2/3 runbooks get a semi-annual review. Done when every tier-1 runbook has a quarterly validation result.
steps.verify: Open the game-day results; pass if each tier-1 runbook's recovery completed verbatim within RTO; any failure shows the runbook flagged 'needs-update' with a 'RUNBOOK-GAP' item and 5-day re-validation.

steps.title: Version review evidence and obtain the SRE check
steps.sop: The Software Engineer tags review evidence in Confluence with the quarter (e.g. 2025-Q3), UTC timestamp, author, and last-reviewed date, referencing the approved orchestration config version from IaC (Terraform state) at review time; the Site Reliability Engineer performs the independent re-performance check with parameters sourced from the DAG definitions and orchestration config export, not memory. Done when evidence is tagged and the SRE check recorded.
steps.verify: Open the quarter's review evidence in Confluence; pass if it carries quarter tag, UTC timestamp, IaC config reference, and a recorded Site Reliability Engineer check.

steps.title: Record Platform Engineering Lead sign-off
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains the Platform Engineering Lead's sign-off on the quarter's runbook currency in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the sign-off is recorded after the game-day results and reconciliation are clean.
steps.verify: Open the quarterly review record; pass if Platform Engineering Lead sign-off is present, dated after the game-day validation results.

steps.title: Register a subject for every producer schema change
steps.sop: The Backend Developer registers or promotes a schema-registry subject (Avro/Protobuf/JSON Schema) in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) for every producer schema change in the domain, setting the compatibility mode on each subject. Done when no producer change ships without a registered subject version.
steps.verify: Open the schema registry in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent); pass if every recent producer change maps to a new subject version with a set compatibility mode.

steps.title: Keep schema definitions versioned in the schemas/ path
steps.sop: The Software Engineer keeps all schema definitions versioned in the schemas/ path of the source code/CI-CD repository, auto-published to the registry by the pipeline. Done when the registry's latest versions match the repo's schemas/ content.
steps.verify: Diff the schemas/ path against the registry's latest subject versions; pass if they match exactly and publication was performed by the pipeline (not manual).

steps.title: Populate catalog metadata for each subject
steps.sop: The Data Engineer populates the data catalog/quality tool for every active topic's subject with: owner, description, compatibility mode, and business-glossary link, with field definitions flowing from the registry subject definitions (field names, types, doc strings) rather than re-typed by hand. Done when no active subject lacks any of the four metadata fields.
steps.verify: Audit catalog entries in the data catalog/quality tool; pass if every active subject shows owner, description, compatibility mode, and glossary link, with technical fields sourced from the registry.

steps.title: Run the daily registry-to-catalog reconciliation
steps.sop: The Software Engineer runs the daily reconciliation in the data catalog/quality tool: registered subjects vs active prod topics (1 key + 1 value subject where applicable) and registry subject count vs catalog dataset count for the domain. Done when the delta is 0 and unmatched subjects/topics are listed for remediation; a topic with data but no registered subject is a hard failure.
steps.verify: Open the daily reconciliation report; pass if subject counts match active topics and catalog datasets exactly (delta 0), with any orphan listed for remediation and no data-bearing topic lacking a subject.

steps.title: Log discoverability failures in the catalog issue queue
steps.sop: The Data Engineer logs subjects failing catalog discoverability rules (missing owner/description) in the issue queue of the data catalog/quality tool, owner = Backend Developer, with remediation within 10 business days. Done when every failing subject has an open issue.
steps.verify: Open the catalog issue queue; pass if each discoverability failure has an issue assigned to the Backend Developer within the 10-business-day window.

steps.title: Roll back unannounced breaking schema changes
steps.sop: If a breaking schema change was published without notice, the Backend Developer rolls back the subject in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) and opens an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket with a 10-business-day remediation SLA. Done when the prior compatible version is restored and the exception logged.
steps.verify: Check the subject's version history; pass if the breaking version is superseded/rolled back and a linked 'SDLC-Exception' ticket exists.

steps.title: Archive the reconciliation report and sync logs
steps.sop: The Software Engineer archives the daily registry-to-catalog reconciliation report (delta 0) in the data catalog/quality tool, with catalog sync run logs retained 12 months with timestamps. Done when the report is archived for the day.
steps.verify: Open the archive in the data catalog/quality tool; pass if the day's reconciliation report is stored and sync logs cover the trailing 12 months.

steps.title: Record Data Steward sign-off on registry currency
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains the Data Steward's sign-off in the data catalog/quality tool confirming every active topic has a current, catalog-discoverable subject with required metadata and compatibility mode. Done when the sign-off is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the sign-off record; pass if Data Steward approval is present and the referenced reconciliation shows 100% coverage with delta 0.

steps.title: Run the monthly completeness sweep in the CMDB
steps.sop: The Software Engineer runs the monthly completeness sweep over all CIs of class 'Application Service' in the CMDB (with a formal reconciliation additionally at each release). Done when every CI in the class has been evaluated this cycle.
steps.verify: Open the sweep run log; pass if it covers 100% of 'Application Service' CIs and is dated within the current month.

steps.title: Complete required attributes on every CI
steps.sop: The Systems Analyst populates each CI in the CMDB with: owning team, technical owner, current deployed version, environment, upstream/downstream dependencies, and required tags (Owner, CostCenter, Environment). Done when 0 CIs are missing owner or version.
steps.verify: Query the CMDB; pass if >= 98% of CIs carry owner and current version, all required tags are present, and 0 CIs lack owner or version outstanding without a task.

steps.title: Reconcile CMDB counts against the deployment registry and SBOM
steps.sop: The Backend Developer reconciles the CMDB service count against the CI/CD deployment registry and the repo list (deployed services in pipeline = CIs in CMDB), investigating any variance > 2%, and checks dependency edges against SBOM output generated from the source repos. Done when the reconciliation report shows variance <= 2% with all exceptions investigated.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation report; pass if CMDB-vs-pipeline variance is <= 2% (with investigations noted) and dependency edges match the SBOM output.

steps.title: Log discrepancies as ServiceNow tasks with disposition
steps.sop: The Software Engineer logs each discrepancy (orphan CIs, stale versions, missing owners) as a task in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with an owner and a disposition (create/update/retire) before the sweep closes; failing CIs route to the owning team with a 10-business-day remediation SLA and unowned CIs escalate to the Platform Engineering Lead for ownership assignment. Done when every discrepancy is ticketed.
steps.verify: Query sweep-linked tasks in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if every discrepancy has a task with owner and disposition, and unowned CIs show the escalation.

steps.title: Link bulk updates to a change record
steps.sop: The Systems Analyst links any bulk inventory update to a ServiceNow change/task record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) referencing the reconciliation run; retire decisions and inventory schema changes require Platform Engineering Lead approval per the CMDB governance RACI, with no self-approval of retirements. Done when all bulk changes trace to a change record.
steps.verify: Open the bulk-update change records; pass if each references the reconciliation run and retirements show a Platform Engineering Lead approval distinct from the requester.

steps.title: Verify the pre/post sweep completeness target
steps.sop: The Software Engineer compares pre- vs post-sweep completeness in the CMDB, confirming attribute completeness improved or held at target (>= 98% of CIs with owner + version), and exports the monthly reconciliation report with date; CMDB records retain last-discovered/last-updated timestamps and discovery job logs are retained. Done when the report is exported and the target met.
steps.verify: Open the monthly report; pass if post-sweep completeness is >= 98% owner + version and the report carries the export date with discovery timestamps intact.

steps.title: Record Tech Lead sign-off on the inventory sweep
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains Tech Lead sign-off on the completed sweep in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the sign-off is recorded against the monthly reconciliation record.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation record; pass if Tech Lead sign-off is present and dated after the completeness report was exported.

steps.title: Log each defect with complete mandatory fields
steps.sop: The QA Analyst logs every defect for the release's components in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps as type 'Defect' with: severity, priority, reproduction steps, environment, linked failing test/build, and assignee — covering unit, integration, UAT, and production sources. Done when the defect record is complete; defects missing severity or repro steps are returned to the reporter and cannot progress to 'In Progress'.
steps.verify: Sample release defects in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if each has severity, priority, repro steps, environment, linked failing test/build, and assignee, and no incomplete defect has moved past 'Open'.

steps.title: Triage defects at the sprint defect-triage session
steps.sop: The Test Lead triages all open defects — including carry-overs from prior releases — each sprint in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps, confirming severity/priority and assignment. Done when every open defect has a current triage decision this sprint.
steps.verify: Open the triage board; pass if no open defect (including carried-over ones) lacks a triage decision dated within the current sprint.

steps.title: Reconcile defects against CI failures and test runs
steps.sop: The QA Analyst reconciles open + closed defect counts in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps against the CI test-failure log and the QA test-run report. Done when no defect exists without a source test/observation and no failing test lacks a defect.
steps.verify: Compare the defect list to the CI failure log and QA run report; pass if the sets reconcile both directions with zero unmatched entries.

steps.title: Deliver each fix through a reviewed pull request
steps.sop: The Software Engineer (with the Backend Developer or UI Developer as appropriate to the component) delivers each defect fix via a reviewed, merged PR and attaches the fix commit SHA to the defect in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps. Done when the defect carries the merged fix reference and related automated tests pass in CI.
steps.verify: Open a fixed defect; pass if it links a merged reviewed PR with the fix commit SHA and the CI run for that commit is green.

steps.title: Re-test and attach verification evidence
steps.sop: The QA Analyst re-tests each fixed defect in the test environment and attaches the passing re-test run to the ticket in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps, confirming the original reproduction no longer occurs. Done when closure evidence (fix SHA, passing re-test, reviewer approval) is on the ticket with timestamps.
steps.verify: Open the closed defect; pass if it holds the fix SHA, a passing re-test run, and reviewer approval — the defect is 'Done' only with all three.

steps.title: Disposition non-fix closures with Tech Lead concurrence
steps.sop: The Test Lead ensures defects dispositioned as won't-fix, duplicate, or not-a-defect carry a documented rationale and recorded Tech Lead concurrence on the ticket in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps before closure. Done when no non-fix closure lacks both.
steps.verify: Query non-fix closures for the release; pass if each shows a written rationale and a Tech Lead concurrence entry prior to the closure transition.

steps.title: Enforce the release defect gate
steps.sop: The Test Lead verifies at release cut in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps: 0 open critical/high (P1/P2) defects, and every medium (P3) defect has either a fix or an approved waiver; a critical defect that cannot be fixed by cut requires an 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Engineering Manager with a documented workaround and a 10-business-day remediation SLA. Done when the gate query returns clean.
steps.verify: Run the release defect query; pass if P1/P2 open count = 0 and every open P3 has a fix or approved waiver, with any deferred critical carrying its 'SDLC-Exception' and workaround.

steps.title: Record Test Lead sign-off and archive the defect summary
steps.sop: The Test Lead records sign-off on the release defect status in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps and archives the release defect summary to the release documentation page. Done when the sign-off and archived summary both exist.
steps.verify: Open the release record; pass if Test Lead sign-off is present and the archived defect summary is linked from the release documentation.

tasks.taskName: Manage event streaming and messaging platform

steps.title: Maintain the production topic inventory with full configuration
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer maintains every production topic in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) with an owner, a schema registered in the schema registry, retention settings, and partition config, keeping the topic inventory matched to the CMDB/service catalog. Done when no production topic lacks any of the four attributes.
steps.verify: Audit the topic inventory in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent); pass if every production topic shows owner, registered schema, retention, and partition config, and the inventory reconciles to the CMDB/service catalog.

steps.title: Keep the platform health dashboards live in Grafana
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer keeps broker-health, consumer-lag, and throughput dashboards live in Grafana against the platform SLOs: 99.9% broker availability, p99 end-to-end latency < 500ms, consumer lag < 10k messages sustained. Done when all three dashboard families render current data with SLO thresholds marked.
steps.verify: Open the dashboards in Grafana; pass if broker health, consumer lag, and throughput panels are live with the 99.9%/500ms/10k SLO thresholds displayed.

steps.title: Reconcile produced vs consumed message counts per topic
steps.sop: The Data Engineer reconciles produced vs consumed message counts per topic in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) within tolerance (no unexplained drops), tracking and reconciling DLQ counts. Done when the period's reconciliation shows no unexplained loss.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation output; pass if per-topic produced/consumed counts balance within tolerance and DLQ counts are accounted for with no unexplained drops.

steps.title: Raise incidents for SLA breaches
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer ensures every SLA breach raises an incident in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with severity set by impact; sustained consumer lag or DLQ growth triggers the runbook and on-call engagement. Done when no breach in the period lacks an incident.
steps.verify: Cross-check breach events against incidents in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if every breach has an incident with impact-based severity and sustained-lag events show runbook/on-call engagement.

steps.title: Log capacity exceptions as SDLC-Exception items
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer logs capacity exceptions as Jira 'SDLC-Exception' items in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), owner = Platform Engineering Lead. Done when each capacity risk identified in the period is ticketed.
steps.verify: Query 'SDLC-Exception' items tagged capacity; pass if every identified capacity exception has one, owned by the Platform Engineering Lead.

steps.title: Track configuration changes via change records
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer records every platform config change (topics, brokers, retention, partitions) via a ServiceNow change record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when no config change exists without a change record.
steps.verify: Sample recent config changes in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent); pass if each has a matching change record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira).

steps.title: Export the monthly SLA and throughput report
steps.sop: The Data Engineer exports the monthly SLA/throughput report (rolling 30-day window) with timestamp to the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), snapshotting the Grafana dashboards for the reporting period; capacity and retention config get a quarterly review. Done when the report and snapshots are stored for the month.
steps.verify: Open the monthly report; pass if it covers the rolling 30 days with timestamp, dashboard snapshots are attached, and the quarterly capacity/retention review is current.

steps.title: Record Platform Engineering Lead sign-off on the monthly review
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer obtains the Platform Engineering Lead's sign-off on the monthly SLA review in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the sign-off is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the monthly review record; pass if Platform Engineering Lead sign-off is present and dated after the report export.

steps.title: Register each partner endpoint in the API gateway
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer registers every third-party/partner endpoint with an active connection agreement (reinsurers, bureaus, payment processors, Guidewire cloud interfaces) in the API gateway (Apigee/Kong/Azure API Management) for production and non-prod, recording endpoint URL, owning team, SLA tier, and IP allowlist. Done when every active-agreement partner has a registered connection.
steps.verify: List connections in the API gateway (Apigee/Kong/Azure API Management); pass if each active partner agreement has an entry with URL, owning team, SLA tier, and IP allowlist.

steps.title: Configure vault-referenced credentials in the IAM platform
steps.sop: The Security Engineer configures each connection's mTLS/API-key credential in Okta / IAM Platform as a vault reference — never inline in config. Done when every partner connection resolves its credential from the vault.
steps.verify: Inspect connection credential config via Okta / IAM Platform; pass if every credential is a vault reference and no inline secret exists in any connection definition.

steps.title: Confirm the pipeline policy gate blocks incomplete connections
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer confirms the pipeline policy gate blocks promotion of any connection record missing endpoint URL, credential reference, owning team, SLA tier, or IP allowlist. Done when a test connection missing a field is rejected by the gate.
steps.verify: Review the policy-gate run for a deliberately incomplete test record; pass if promotion was blocked and the gate log names the missing field.

steps.title: Reconcile gateway connections to partner agreements
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer reconciles the count of configured connections in the API gateway (Apigee/Kong/Azure API Management) 1:1 against active partner agreements in the CLM repository and CMDB CI records. Done when variance is 0 or every delta has an open Jira 'INT-Recon' ticket explaining it.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation report; pass if gateway connections match active agreements 1:1, or each delta references an open 'INT-Recon' ticket.

steps.title: Commit the connection config export with the change record
steps.sop: The Software Engineer exports and commits the connection configuration with git SHA and ISO-8601 timestamp, and records the gateway change in an ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) change ticket retained 3 years per the audit-trail policy. Done when both the commit and the change ticket exist.
steps.verify: Open the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if it links the committed config export with git SHA and ISO-8601 timestamp and carries the 3-year retention classification.

steps.title: Monitor connection health and ticket failures
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer monitors the trailing-90-day connection-health telemetry so failed handshakes, cert-expiry warnings, and rate-limit breaches raise incidents tagged 'partner-connectivity' in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), with disposition (fixed / accepted-risk / partner-side) recorded within the severity's SLA; connections are re-verified each release and on any partner certificate rotation. Done when monitoring is active and every event is ticketed.
steps.verify: Query 'partner-connectivity' incidents; pass if each handshake/cert/rate-limit event in the window has an incident with a disposition recorded inside its severity SLA.

steps.title: Record Integration Architect sign-off on the connectivity estate
steps.sop: The Integration Engineer obtains the Integration Architect's sign-off on the reconciled connectivity estate in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the sign-off is recorded for the release cycle.
steps.verify: Open the cycle's connectivity review record; pass if Integration Architect sign-off is present and dated after the reconciliation.

steps.title: Assemble the quarterly engagement extract from Confluence
steps.sop: The Software Engineer assembles the engagement extract for the most recent full quarter (e.g. 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30) from the Confluence 'ENG' space and docs portal analytics, covering page views, unique readers, search queries, and helpfulness ratings across all published runbooks, ADRs, and how-to articles. Done when every published article active in the quarter appears in the extract.
steps.verify: Compare the extract's article census to the published-article list in Confluence; pass if all active articles for the quarter are present with views, readers, search, and rating data.

steps.title: Validate extract rows against the required field set
steps.sop: The Software Engineer validates each extract row for: article id, period, views, unique_users, avg_rating, and search_hits, excluding rows with null article id or period as invalid. Done when the cleaned extract contains only fully-keyed rows.
steps.verify: Profile the extract; pass if 0 rows with null article id or period remain and every row carries all six fields.

steps.title: Load the extract into the BI platform
steps.sop: The Software Engineer loads the cleaned extract into the BI/reporting platform and archives the underlying extract to the data warehouse engagement schema. Done when the load completes and the archive copy exists.
steps.verify: Open the BI/reporting platform dataset; pass if the quarter's extract is loaded, row counts match the source, and the warehouse archive copy is present.

steps.title: Reconcile extract totals to source analytics
steps.sop: The Software Engineer reconciles in the BI/reporting platform: the sum of per-article views to the platform-level total pageview count within +/- 1%, and the unique-user total to the SSO analytics feed. Done when both reconciliations are inside tolerance; a larger variance triggers a data-quality check.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation result; pass if per-article view sums are within +/- 1% of the platform total and unique users match the SSO feed.

steps.title: Remediate reconciliation failures before publication
steps.sop: On reconciliation failure, the Software Engineer holds dashboard publication, opens a data-quality Jira item assigned to the Data Engineer, backfills the missing analytics load, and re-runs the reconciliation, all within a 10-business-day resolution SLA. Done when the re-run passes.
steps.verify: If a failure occurred, open the data-quality item; pass if the dashboard was withheld until the backfilled re-run reconciled within +/- 1% inside the SLA.

steps.title: Publish the quarterly engagement dashboard
steps.sop: The Software Engineer publishes the engagement dashboard in the BI/reporting platform with report version, refresh timestamp, and month-over-month trend. Done when the dashboard is live showing the quarter with MoM trend.
steps.verify: Open the dashboard in the BI/reporting platform; pass if it shows the quarter's metrics with report version, refresh timestamp, and month-over-month trend panels.

steps.title: Flag low-engagement content for review
steps.sop: The Software Engineer flags articles with 0 views or an average rating below 3 and raises a Jira 'docs-review' item to each content owner with a 10-business-day triage window. Done when every flagged article has a review item.
steps.verify: Cross-check the low-engagement list against 'docs-review' items; pass if every 0-view or sub-3-rating article has one assigned to its content owner.

steps.title: Record Tech Lead approval of the published report
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains the Tech Lead's approval of the metric definitions and published dashboard (delegate in their absence: Engineering Manager, per the report governance page). Done when the approval is recorded for the quarter.
steps.verify: Open the report governance record; pass if the quarter's approval is attributed to the Tech Lead or the documented Engineering Manager delegate.

steps.title: Verify the PR satisfies every merge-gate condition
steps.sop: The Software Engineer verifies in the source code/CI-CD repository that the single approved pull request targeting mainline (main/develop) has: >= 2 approvals, all conversations resolved, a linked Jira work item, green required checks (build, unit, SAST, coverage), and a Conventional Commit title — branch protection blocks the merge until all are true. Done when the PR shows all gates green.
steps.verify: Open the PR in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if it shows >= 2 approvals, 0 unresolved conversations, a linked work item, all required checks green, and a Conventional Commit title.

steps.title: Merge the pull request to mainline
steps.sop: The Software Engineer merges the approved PR to mainline in the source code/CI-CD repository within the current sprint/release-train iteration, containing only reviewed and CI-green changes. Done when the merge completes.
steps.verify: Open the mainline branch history; pass if the merge commit for the PR is present and dated within the iteration.

steps.title: Verify the merged content matches the approved PR
steps.sop: The Backend Developer verifies in the source code/CI-CD repository that the post-merge mainline HEAD SHA equals the merge commit and that the commit count and diff on main match the approved PR with no extra commits added. Done when the comparison is exact.
steps.verify: Compare mainline HEAD to the merge commit and the PR diff; pass if the SHAs match and no commit exists on main that was not in the approved PR.

steps.title: Confirm the post-merge CI run on main is green
steps.sop: The UI Developer confirms the CI pipeline re-runs on main in the source code/CI-CD repository after the merge and completes green. Done when the main-branch pipeline run for the merge commit passes.
steps.verify: Open the CI run for the merge commit on main; pass if all stages are green with no skipped required checks.

steps.title: Record the merge evidence with UTC timestamp
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records the merge commit SHA, PR number, approvers, and CI run URL in the PR and the release notes in the source code/CI-CD repository, timestamped in UTC, with the branch-protection audit log retained. Done when the evidence set is complete.
steps.verify: Open the PR/release notes; pass if merge SHA, PR number, approver names, CI run URL, and UTC timestamp are all recorded.

steps.title: Log any branch-protection override as an SDLC-Exception
steps.sop: If any branch-protection override occurred (admin merge, bypassed check), the Software Engineer raises an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket owned by the Engineering Manager with justification and a 10-business-day review, logged in the exception register. Done when every override is ticketed — or confirmed that none occurred.
steps.verify: Check the branch-protection audit log for overrides; pass if none occurred, or each override has a matching 'SDLC-Exception' with justification in the exception register.

steps.title: Record Tech Lead sign-off on the completed merge
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains Tech Lead sign-off on the completed merge in the source code/CI-CD repository. Done when the sign-off is recorded on the PR or release record.
steps.verify: Open the PR/release record; pass if Tech Lead sign-off is present and dated after the green post-merge CI run.

tasks.taskName: Model pipeline DAG with task dependencies

steps.title: Draft the pipeline design diagram in the docs folder
steps.sop: The Data Engineer drafts the design diagram (Mermaid) in the /docs folder of the source code/CI-CD repository for the pipeline named on the design ticket, showing all tasks, their upstream/downstream dependencies, trigger rules, and SLAs, during the current design sprint. Done when the diagram covers every task and edge of the intended pipeline.
steps.verify: Open /docs in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if the Mermaid diagram exists for the named pipeline and depicts all tasks, edges, trigger rules, and SLAs.

steps.title: Define the DAG with complete per-task attributes
steps.sop: The Software Engineer defines the DAG in the source code/CI-CD repository ('data-platform-orchestration' repo) specifying for every task: task_id, dependency edges, trigger_rule, retries, SLA, and owner. Done when no task is missing any of the six attributes.
steps.verify: Review the DAG definition; pass if every task declares task_id, edges, trigger_rule, retries, SLA, and owner.

steps.title: Validate acyclicity in the orchestrator
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer parses the DAG in the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect), which validates acyclicity. Done when the DAG parses with 0 cycles and no import errors.
steps.verify: Open the parse result in the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect); pass if the DAG loads with 0 cycles and 0 errors.

steps.title: Reconcile the DAG model against the design diagram
steps.sop: The Backend Developer reconciles the count of tasks and edges in the DAG definition against the source design diagram in the source code/CI-CD repository, confirming every terminal task has exactly one defined completion signal. Done when counts match and terminal signals are unique.
steps.verify: Compare DAG task/edge counts to the diagram; pass if they match exactly and each terminal task shows exactly one completion signal.

steps.title: Model external triggers as ExternalTaskSensors
steps.sop: The Software Engineer documents cross-pipeline dependencies that cannot be modeled as direct edges as ExternalTaskSensors in the DAG definition in the source code/CI-CD repository, each with a disposition note; unresolved coupling is logged as an 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Tech Lead. Done when every external dependency is either a sensor or an exception ticket.
steps.verify: Review the DAG's external dependencies; pass if each is an ExternalTaskSensor with disposition note, or has a linked 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Tech Lead.

steps.title: Commit the DAG and diagram tagged with the design ticket
steps.sop: The Software Engineer commits the DAG definition together with the design diagram in /docs via a pull request in the source code/CI-CD repository, tagged with the design-ticket ID and UTC timestamp. Done when the PR is open with both artifacts.
steps.verify: Open the PR; pass if it contains the DAG file and the /docs diagram, tagged with the design-ticket ID and a UTC timestamp.

steps.title: Record Tech Lead sign-off on the DAG model
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains Tech Lead approval on the PR in the source code/CI-CD repository before implementation begins. Done when the approval is recorded and the PR merged.
steps.verify: Open the merged PR; pass if Tech Lead approval is present and predates any implementation commits for the pipeline.

steps.title: Draft the process and data flow diagrams for the epic
steps.sop: The Business Analyst drafts the flow diagrams (BPMN/sequence plus data flow) for feature/epic PROJ-#### against the current requirements baseline, authored as diagrams-as-code and mirrored to Confluence. Done when both the process flows and data flows for the proposed solution exist in draft.
steps.verify: Open the epic's flow page in Confluence; pass if BPMN/sequence and data-flow diagrams are both present and reference the current requirements baseline.

steps.title: Annotate flows with actors, systems, and trust boundaries
steps.sop: The Business Analyst annotates each diagram in Confluence with: actors/roles, systems, data entities and their classification, trust boundaries, and error/exception paths, labeling every PII data element, using the approved notation (BPMN + C4/sequence). Done when every diagram carries all annotation categories.
steps.verify: Inspect each diagram; pass if actors, systems, classified data entities, trust boundaries, and error paths are shown, every PII element is labeled, and the notation is BPMN + C4/sequence.

steps.title: Verify requirement-to-flow traceability
steps.sop: The Software Engineer verifies in the requirements matrix that every requirement in the epic maps to at least one flow step (100% traceability). Done when 0 requirements are unmapped.
steps.verify: Open the requirements matrix; pass if each requirement row references >= 1 flow step in the diagrams — 100% coverage.

steps.title: Verify flow systems exist in the architecture inventory
steps.sop: The Solutions Architect verifies that every system touched in the flows exists in the CMDB/architecture inventory. Done when no diagram references a system absent from the inventory.
steps.verify: Cross-check the diagrams' system list against the CMDB/architecture inventory; pass if every system resolves to an inventory entry.

steps.title: Log open questions in the RAID register
steps.sop: The Business Analyst logs open questions and assumptions in the RAID/assumptions register with owner and target resolution date, flagging any unresolved flow gaps before design sign-off. Done when no open question exists outside the register.
steps.verify: Open the RAID register; pass if every open question/assumption from the modeling work appears with owner and target date, and flow gaps are flagged.

steps.title: Publish the versioned diagrams to Confluence
steps.sop: The Business Analyst publishes the diagrams to Confluence, with the diagram source committed as diagrams-as-code so each revision is timestamped, and the Confluence render showing version and reviewer sign-off date; diagrams are updated whenever requirements change. Done when the published version matches the committed source.
steps.verify: Open the Confluence page; pass if the rendered diagrams show a version and sign-off date and match the latest committed diagram source revision.

steps.title: Review flows with the Solutions Architect and record sign-off
steps.sop: The Business Analyst walks the Solutions Architect and Software Engineer through the flows and records the review outcome and Business Analyst sign-off on the Confluence page. Done when the documented-and-reviewed condition is met.
steps.verify: Open the page's review record; pass if the Solutions Architect review and the Business Analyst sign-off are both recorded with dates.

tasks.taskName: Monitor pipeline run status and SLA breaches

steps.title: Build the per-pipeline monitoring dashboard in Grafana
steps.sop: The Software Engineer builds the dashboard in Grafana exposing, for every in-scope pipeline: last run status, start/end time, duration vs SLA, queue depth, and error rate. Done when all scheduled and event-driven pipelines in the orchestrator render on the dashboard.
steps.verify: Open the dashboard in Grafana; pass if every in-scope pipeline shows the five required panels (status, times, duration vs SLA, queue depth, error rate).

steps.title: Version and approve the alert ruleset
steps.sop: The Data Engineer versions alert thresholds and SLA definitions in the monitoring-config repo with SLA targets sourced from the service catalog / data-product SLA definitions in the CMDB (no hard-coded values outside the config repo), obtaining Platform Engineering Lead approval before activation; the current version is tagged and referenced by the dashboards in Grafana. Done when the approved, tagged ruleset is live.
steps.verify: Open the monitoring-config repo tag referenced by the Grafana dashboards; pass if the ruleset is approved by the Platform Engineering Lead and thresholds trace to the CMDB SLA definitions.

steps.title: Configure alert sensitivity and criticality tiers
steps.sop: The Data Engineer configures alerting in Grafana: warn at 80% of SLA duration, breach at 100%; queue-depth warn at > 50 pending, critical at > 200; tuned to keep the false-positive rate < 5%. Pipelines feeding regulatory, financial, or customer-facing outputs are P1 and internal/dev pipelines P3, distinguished by the criticality tag in the CMDB/catalog. Done when the thresholds and tiers are active.
steps.verify: Inspect the alert rules in Grafana; pass if the 80%/100% SLA thresholds, 50/200 queue thresholds, and P1/P3 criticality mapping are all configured.

steps.title: Wire automatic incident creation for failures and breaches
steps.sop: The Production Support Engineer wires the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) so a failed run or SLA breach auto-creates an incident routed to the on-call Data Engineer with severity by impact and a runbook link, and an unresolved P1 escalates to the Platform Engineering Lead after 30 minutes. Done when a test breach produces an incident with correct routing.
steps.verify: Trigger a test breach; pass if an incident auto-creates in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with runbook link, on-call routing, and the 30-minute P1 escalation rule configured.

steps.title: Reconcile expected vs actual run counts
steps.sop: The Data Engineer reconciles expected vs actual run counts per schedule in the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect) so missed runs = 0, and reconciles records processed against source control totals at +/- 0% for critical feeds before downstream consumption. Done when the reconciliation is clean for the period.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation output; pass if scheduled vs actual runs match (0 missed) and critical-feed record counts match source totals exactly.

steps.title: Run the 7-day monitoring-coverage observation test
steps.sop: The Software Engineer runs a 7-day observation over all in-scope pipeline runs: 100% of runs must appear on the dashboard with a status and every failure/SLA breach must generate an alert within 60 seconds. Any silent failure or missed alert raises a P2 monitoring-gap incident owned by the Site Reliability Engineer with the alert rule fixed within 2 business days and root cause logged. Done when the observation window closes with no uncured gaps.
steps.verify: Open the observation report; pass if run-status coverage is 100%, all failures alerted within 60s, and any gap shows a resolved P2 incident with root cause.

steps.title: Retain monitoring evidence and publish the weekly coverage report
steps.sop: The Production Support Engineer retains run history, alert events, and acknowledgements in the orchestrator and the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with UTC timestamps and run IDs (90-day hot retention, 12-month archive), and publishes the weekly monitoring-coverage report to ServiceNow. Done when the week's report is filed with retention in place.
steps.verify: Open the weekly coverage report in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if it is current, and spot-checked alert events show UTC timestamps, run IDs, and the retention policy applied.

steps.title: Record Platform Engineering Lead sign-off on monitoring
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains the Platform Engineering Lead's sign-off in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) that monitoring is active per acceptance criteria (100% visibility, 60-second alerting, < 5% false positives), with the Site Reliability Engineer's independent check recorded. Done when the sign-off is captured.
steps.verify: Open the monitoring acceptance record; pass if Platform Engineering Lead sign-off and the SRE independent check are both recorded against the acceptance criteria.

steps.title: Expose the three required metric series per topic
steps.sop: The Data Engineer exposes consumer-lag, partition-skew, and end-to-end latency series for every production Kafka topic and consumer group feeding the lakehouse landing zone (plus the Flink/Spark Structured Streaming jobs reading them) from the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent). Done when no topic is missing any of the three series; a topic missing one is flagged red on the pipeline health dashboard.
steps.verify: Query the metric series per topic; pass if 100% of production topics expose lag, partition-skew, and latency series, with any gap showing the red flag.

steps.title: Build the Streaming Pipeline Health dashboard
steps.sop: The Software Engineer builds the 'Streaming Pipeline Health' dashboard in Grafana (folder: Data Engineering) with 90 days of metric history retention and alerts evaluating on 1-minute windows, running 24x7. Done when the dashboard renders all in-scope topics live.
steps.verify: Open 'Streaming Pipeline Health' in Grafana under Data Engineering; pass if all in-scope topics render with 90-day history and 1-minute alert evaluation configured.

steps.title: Bind alert rules to each telemetry metric
steps.sop: The Data Engineer binds at least one alert rule per metric in Grafana with thresholds: consumer lag < 10,000 messages sustained, p99 end-to-end latency < 5s, 0 partitions in a stalled state; a metric exceeding threshold for > 5 consecutive minutes without a firing alert is a monitoring failure. Done when every metric on every topic has a bound alert rule.
steps.verify: Inspect the alert rules in Grafana; pass if each topic's lag, latency, and partition metrics have bound rules at the 10k/5s/0-stalled thresholds.

steps.title: Configure the 15-minute landing reconciliation
steps.sop: The Data Engineer configures the reconciliation comparing records produced to source topics in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) with records landed in the lakehouse per 15-minute bucket, at a 0.1% tolerance, with a sustained breach raising a P2 alert. Done when the reconciliation runs on schedule with the alert bound.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation panel; pass if 15-minute buckets compare produced vs landed within 0.1% and the sustained-breach P2 alert rule is active.

steps.title: Wire breach incidents with disposition tracking
steps.sop: The Site Reliability Engineer wires each threshold breach to auto-create a ServiceNow incident tagged 'streaming-pipeline', with disposition (resolved / false-positive / suppressed-with-reason) recorded before closure; on alert the on-call SRE follows the linked runbook, and if lag is unrecoverable within the 30-minute SLA escalates to the Software Engineer (owner) and opens a P1 with the consumer-group offset snapshot attached. Done when the incident automation and escalation path are active.
steps.verify: Trigger a test breach; pass if an incident auto-creates tagged 'streaming-pipeline' with runbook link, and closed incidents show a recorded disposition.

steps.title: Run the synthetic lag-injection validation
steps.sop: The Site Reliability Engineer runs a synthetic lag-injection test on one non-prod topic, alongside observation of a representative peak-load window (e.g. the daily batch-catch-up spike). Done when the injected lag fires the alert within the evaluation window and peak-load telemetry stays observable.
steps.verify: Open the injection test results; pass if the alert fired for the injected lag and the peak-window observation shows no metric dropout.

steps.title: Version the dashboard JSON and alert rules in the repo
steps.sop: The Software Engineer stores the Grafana dashboard JSON and alert rules at /observability/streaming/ in the source code/CI-CD repository, with alert-firing history and on-call acknowledgements retained 90 days in the alerting platform and exported to the ITSM incident record. Done when the committed config matches what is deployed.
steps.verify: Diff /observability/streaming/ in the source code/CI-CD repository against the live Grafana config; pass if they match and the 90-day alert-history retention is confirmed.

steps.title: Record Site Reliability Engineer sign-off on observability
steps.sop: The Software Engineer obtains the Site Reliability Engineer's sign-off that telemetry is observable: lag, partition utilization, and end-to-end latency live for every prod topic with at least one bound alert rule each and a 90-day retention window. Done when the sign-off is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the observability acceptance record; pass if SRE sign-off is present and the acceptance evidence shows all three metrics live per topic with bound alerts.

tasks.taskName: Obtain QA sign-off on release candidate

steps.title: Pin the release-candidate scope on the Jira release
steps.sop: The Test Lead records on the Jira release in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) the exact immutable build artifact (version tag) and its full mandatory test scope — unit, integration, contract, regression, security, and performance suites — with each suite's latest run tied to the build SHA and the build timestamp captured for the RC-cut-to-go/no-go window. Done when the release record identifies the build and all six suites.
steps.verify: Open the Jira release; pass if it names the immutable build tag and links all six suite runs, each tied to the same build SHA.

steps.title: Verify every exit criterion on the RC
steps.sop: The QA Analyst verifies against the release record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira): 0 open blocker/critical defects; code coverage >= 80% on changed lines and >= 90% on critical paths; 100% of the regression suite automated and passing; SAST/DAST with 0 critical/high findings (<= 5 medium with waivers); performance within baseline SLA; and UAT sign-off attached. Done when all exit-criteria fields are populated and passing.
steps.verify: Open the exit-criteria checklist; pass if all six criteria show passing values with evidence links — no empty field and no unmet gate without an approved exception.

steps.title: Reconcile test execution and defect counts
steps.sop: The QA Analyst reconciles in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira): planned vs executed test cases with delta = 0 for mandatory suites, and defect counts in the test-management tool against the Jira release defect query (blocker/critical = 0). Done when both reconciliations are exact.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation results; pass if planned = executed for every mandatory suite and the defect counts match across tools with 0 open blocker/critical.

steps.title: Run the pre/post baseline comparison
steps.sop: The Software Engineer runs the comparison for the RC build: full regression passes with 0 new failures vs the prior release baseline, performance benchmark within +/- 10% of the established baseline, and no coverage regression on changed lines. Done when the comparison report is attached to the release.
steps.verify: Open the comparison report on the release; pass if regression shows 0 new failures vs baseline, performance is within +/- 10%, and changed-line coverage did not regress.

steps.title: Log waivers as SDLC-Exception items
steps.sop: The Test Lead logs every waived defect or accepted medium security finding as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with disposition and business justification, owner = Engineering Manager, 10-business-day remediation SLA; unresolved blockers/criticals veto sign-off, and only an approved conditional waiver with a dated remediation plan permits release. Done when every risk-accepted item is ticketed.
steps.verify: Query 'SDLC-Exception' items for the release; pass if each waiver has disposition, justification, Engineering Manager owner, and a dated remediation plan — and no unwaived blocker/critical remains.

steps.title: Export the QA sign-off evidence package
steps.sop: The Test Lead exports the sign-off package — exit-criteria checklist, coverage report, security scan results, and test summary report — to the compliance evidence repository as 'qa-signoff-<release>-<yyyymmdd>.pdf' with build SHA and reviewer signature, retained 7 years. Done when the file is stored with the correct name and contents.
steps.verify: Open the compliance evidence repository; pass if 'qa-signoff-<release>-<yyyymmdd>.pdf' exists containing all four artifacts, the build SHA, and the reviewer signature.

steps.title: Link the change record to the release and evidence
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer links the ServiceNow change/release record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) to the Jira release and the immutable build tag, referencing the QA sign-off evidence ID and the CI/CD pipeline run URL, with the target deployment date recorded. Done when the change record carries all four references.
steps.verify: Open the change record; pass if it links the Jira release, build tag, sign-off evidence ID, and pipeline run URL, with the target deployment date set.

steps.title: Document the Go/No-Go decision on the Jira release
steps.sop: The Test Lead documents the Go/No-Go decision (Approved / Conditional / Rejected) on the Jira release in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) and in the release readiness review minutes, with a residual-risk statement and any conditions; on FAIL, sign-off is withheld and deployment blocked. Done when the decision, risk statement, and conditions are recorded.
steps.verify: Open the Jira release and readiness minutes; pass if the decision value, residual-risk statement, and conditions (if Conditional) are all documented.

steps.title: Distribute the sign-off and record the independent approval
steps.sop: The Test Lead distributes the sign-off to the Release Manager, Product Owner, DevOps Engineer, delivery squad, and Operations/Support via the Jira release comment in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) and the #release-readiness channel, capturing the recipient list in the review minutes; the approver must be the Test Lead (delegates: QA Analyst first, Engineering Manager second when the Test Lead is unavailable > 1 business day) and must be independent of the change author, with any delegation logged in the minutes. Done when distribution and the independent approval are both recorded.
steps.verify: Open the release comment and minutes; pass if the recipient list matches the required distribution, the approver is the Test Lead or a documented delegate, and the approver differs from the change author.
